work: Enarratio in librum Nehemiæ, qui dicitur liber secundus Esdræ
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. V (Montreuil)

1.title: Elucidatio capituli primi: Verba Nehemiæ filii Helchiæ
1.title_en: Explanation of the first chapter: The words of Nehemias the son of Helchias

paras.t: Verba Nehemiæ filii Helchiæ, supple, hæc sunt quæ sequuntur, quæ ab eo conscripta sunt: et fuit de stirpe sacerdotali. Et factum est in mense Casleu: qui apud Hebræos (secundum Josephum) vocatur Sileos, apud Latinos December; anno vicesimo regni Artaxerxis, et ego eram in Susis castro, id est in fortalitio quodam urbis illius, quæ fuit metropolis regni Persarum. Vel per castrum, intelligitur civitas ipsa instar castri fortissima, ut dictum est plenius super Esdram.
paras.en: [[1:1|The words of Nehemiah the son of Helchias|Verba Nehemiæ filii Helchiæ]]: supply, *are these that follow*, which were written by him; and he was of priestly stock. [[1:1|And it came to pass in the month of Casleu|Et factum est in mense Casleu]], which among the Hebrews (according to Josephus) is called Sileos [the margin corrects this to *Chisleus*], among the Latins December; [[1:1|in the twentieth year|anno vicesimo]] of the reign of Artaxerxes, [[1:1|as I was in the castle of Susa|et ego eram in Susis castro]], that is, in a certain fortress of that city, which was the capital of the kingdom of the Persians. Or by *castle* is meant the city itself, very strong like a castle, as was said more fully on Esdras[[1 Esd 6:2||]].

paras.t: Et venit ad me Hanani unus de fratribus meis, id est cognatis. Quod dictum est, Ad me, non est (ut fertur) de textu. Ipse et viri ex Juda, id est ex tribu Juda, vel ex populo Judæorum habitantium in Judæa. Et interrogavi eos de Judæis, qui remanserant et supererant de captivitate, id est, qui adhuc vixerunt, et in Judæa morabantur, reversi ex Babylonica captivitate, seu nati ex illis reversis, et de Jerusalem, id est, de statu civitatis Jerusalem eos specialiter interrogavi. Refert Josephus, quod viri isti quasi peregrini ad urbem Susa declinaverunt. Obviavitque eis Nehemias ante metropolim, audiensque eos Hebraice colloquentes, interrogavit eos quæ dicta sunt.
paras.en: And there [[1:2|came|Et venit]] to me [[1:2|Hanani one of my brethren|Hanani unus de fratribus meis]], that is, of my kinsmen. What is said, *to me*, is not (so it is said) part of the text. [[1:2|he and some men of Juda|Ipse et viri ex Juda]], that is, of the tribe of Juda, or of the people of the Jews dwelling in Judæa. [[1:2|and I asked them concerning the Jews|Et interrogavi eos de Judæis]], [[1:2|that remained and were left of the captivity|qui remanserant et supererant de captivitate]], that is, who were still alive and dwelling in Judæa, having returned from the Babylonian captivity, or born of those who returned, [[1:2|and concerning Jerusalem|et de Jerusalem]], that is, I asked them especially about the state of the city of Jerusalem. Josephus relates that these men, as travellers, turned aside to the city of Susa; and Nehemias met them before the capital, and hearing them talking together in Hebrew, asked them what has been told.

paras.t: Et dixerunt mihi: Qui remanserunt, et relicti sunt de captivitate in provincia, in afflictione magna sunt, et in opprobrio: qui a Samaritanis et circumjacentibus gentibus graviter vexabantur et spernebantur. Imo, ut in Scholastica fertur historia, et ex Josepho sumptum est, per dies sustinebant impetum hostium, noctibus quoque intrabant latrunculi, et plateas Jerusalem implebant cadaveribus mortuorum. Et murus Jerusalem dissipatus est, et portæ ejus combustæ sunt igni. Circa hoc scribit quidam: A tempore quo Nabuzardan incendit civitatem, et muros ejus dirupit, non fuerat data licentia reædificandi eam, sed solum templum et pertinentia ad ipsum, per Cyrum et Darium. Sicque juxta expositionem istius, quod hic dicitur de dissipatione murorum Jerusalem, et de combustione portarum ipsius, intelligitur de destructione et combustione facta per Nabuzardan principem militiæ Chaldæorum. Sed error dicti istius, supra in expositione libri Esther ostensus est; et ex expositione primi libri Esdræ patet. Nempe, quod civitas Jerusalem de Cyri regis licentia reædificaretur, Deus per Isaiam evidenter prædixit, ubi de Cyro loquens: Ipse, inquit, ædificabit civitatem meam. Et asserit idem Josephus. Denique destructionem murorum Jerusalem per Chaldæos factam Nehemias non ignoravit, nec aliquis Judæorum. Quod autem scriptura ista loquatur de dissipatione murorum Jerusalem Nehemiam latente, constat tam ex isto, quam ex sequenti capitulo.
paras.en: [[1:3|And they said to me|Et dixerunt mihi]]: [[1:3|They that have remained, and are left of the captivity|Qui remanserunt, et relicti sunt de captivitate]] [[1:3|in the province|in provincia]], [[1:3|are in great affliction, and reproach|in afflictione magna sunt, et in opprobrio]]: for they were grievously harassed and scorned by the Samaritans and the nations round about. Indeed, as is related in the Scholastic History, and taken from Josephus, by day they bore the onslaught of enemies, and by night too robbers came in, and filled the streets of Jerusalem with the bodies of the dead [this passage is damaged at the edge of the column in the OCR, and some words are read by the sense]. [[1:3|and the wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and the gates thereof are burnt with fire|Et murus Jerusalem dissipatus est, et portæ ejus combustæ sunt igni]]. On this someone writes: “From the time when Nabuzardan burnt the city and broke down its walls, leave had not been given to rebuild it, but only the temple and what belonged to it, by Cyrus and Darius.” And so according to this man's exposition, what is said here of the breaking down of the walls of Jerusalem and the burning of its gates is understood of the destruction and burning done by Nabuzardan, the captain of the army of the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:9||]][[4 Kings 25:10||]]. But the error of this saying was shown above in the exposition of the book of Esther, and is plain from the exposition of the first book of Esdras[[1 Esd 1:3||]]. For God clearly foretold by Isaias that the city of Jerusalem would be rebuilt by king Cyrus's leave, where, speaking of Cyrus, He says: *He*, says He, [[Is 45:13|shall build my city|ædificabit civitatem meam]]. And Josephus asserts the same. Moreover, Nehemias was not ignorant of the destruction of the walls of Jerusalem made by the Chaldeans, nor was any of the Jews. And that this scripture speaks of a breaking down of the walls of Jerusalem that Nehemias did not know of is clear both from this chapter and from the following one.

paras.t: Subditur enim: Quumque audissem verba hujuscemodi, sedi et flevi, et luxi diebus multis; et jejunabam, et orabam. Bona namque est oratio cum jejunio, prout angelus Raphael ait Tobiæ. Sed et lacrimæ, quæ ex caritatis fervore, seu vera contritione devotionisque pietate procedunt, orationem faciunt esse fortissimam. Insuper, sequenti capitulo loquitur Nehemias ad regem: Quare non mœreat vultus meus, quia civitas domus sepulcrorum patris mei deserta est, et portæ ejus combustæ sunt? Unde probatur, ista intelligenda esse de nova destructione, quam ante nescierat Nehemias. Denique, quod Jerusalem sub Zorobabel et Esdra fuerit aliqualiter reædificata, patet ex dictis in Esdra, in cujus libro primo scriptum est: Civitatem Jerusalem reædificant exstruentes muros ejus.
paras.en: For it is added: [[1:4|And when I had heard these words|Quumque audissem verba hujuscemodi]], [[1:4|I sat down, and wept, and mourned for many days|sedi et flevi, et luxi diebus multis]]; [[1:4|and I fasted, and prayed|et jejunabam, et orabam]]. For prayer is good with fasting, as the angel Raphael says to Tobias[[Tob 12:8||]]. And tears too, which proceed from the fervour of charity, or from true contrition and the tenderness of devotion, make prayer most strong. Moreover, in the following chapter Nehemias says to the king: [[2 Esd 2:3|why should not my countenance be sorrowful, seeing the city of the place of the sepulchres of my fathers is desolate, and the gates thereof are burnt with fire?|Quare non mœreat vultus meus, quia civitas domus sepulcrorum patris mei deserta est, et portæ ejus combustæ sunt?]] Hence it is proved that these things are to be understood of a new destruction, which Nehemias had not known of before. Lastly, that Jerusalem had been rebuilt in some measure under Zorobabel and Esdras is plain from what was said on Esdras, in whose first book it is written of the city of Jerusalem: [[1 Esd 4:12|which they are building, setting up the ramparts thereof|reædificant exstruentes muros ejus]].

paras.t: Et dixi: Quæso, Domine Deus cæli, id est universorum cælestium corporum, ac supernorum spirituum. Nam sicut per terram intelliguntur frequenter habitantes in terra, juxta illud, Omnis terra adoret te, Deus; ita per cælum, habitantes in cælo. Fortis, quia omnipotens; magne, quoniam infinitus es in omni perfectione; atque terribilis, videlicet justus et imperscrutabilis, in cujus manus incidere, est valde metuendum; qui custodis pactum, id est promissum, seu amicitiæ fœdus ac jus, et misericordiam his qui te diligunt, et custodiunt mandata tua: quibus fideliter imples et pie donas quod promisisti. Fiant aures tuæ auscultantes, et oculi tui aperti, ut audias orationem servi tui, quam ego oro coram te hodie nocte ac die, pro filiis Israel servis tuis. Loquitur autem Scriptura de supersimplicissimo et invariabili Deo affectu et more humano, quum tamen aures et oculi Dei, non sint nisi sapientia ejus, omnia noscens ac intuens, ut sit sensus: Per effectum exauditionis orationis meæ, ostende te nosse ac intueri meam orationem, qua oro pro servis tuis. Multum etenim placet Deo amor boni communis, et oratio fusa ex tali amore. Et confiteor pro peccatis eorum, quibus peccaverunt tibi, id est, confiteor eos peccasse, ut digneris eis ignoscere.
paras.en: [[1:5|And I said: I beseech thee, O Lord God of heaven|Et dixi: Quæso, Domine Deus cæli]], that is, of all the heavenly bodies and of the spirits above. For as by *earth* are often understood those who dwell on the earth, according to that saying, [[Ps 65:4|Let all the earth adore thee|Omnis terra adoret te]], O God; so by *heaven*, those who dwell in heaven. [[1:5|strong|Fortis]], because almighty; [[1:5|great|magne]], since thou art infinite in every perfection; [[1:5|and terrible|atque terribilis]], namely just and unsearchable, into whose hands to fall is greatly to be feared[[Heb 10:31||]]; [[1:5|who keepest covenant|qui custodis pactum]], that is, a promise, or the bond and right of friendship, [[1:5|and mercy with those that love thee, and keep thy commandments|et misericordiam his qui te diligunt, et custodiunt mandata tua]]: for whom thou faithfully fulfillest and graciously grantest what thou hast promised. [[1:6|Let thy ears be attentive, and thy eyes open|Fiant aures tuæ auscultantes, et oculi tui aperti]], [[1:6|to hear the prayer of thy servant, which I pray before thee now, night and day, for the children of Israel thy servants|ut audias orationem servi tui, quam ego oro coram te hodie nocte ac die, pro filiis Israel servis tuis]]. Now Scripture speaks of the most utterly simple and unchangeable God after the affection and manner of men, though the ears and eyes of God are nothing but His wisdom, knowing and beholding all things; so that the sense is: by the effect of hearing my prayer, show that thou knowest and beholdest my prayer, which I pray for thy servants. For the love of the common good is very pleasing to God, and prayer poured out from such love. [[1:6|and I confess the sins|Et confiteor pro peccatis eorum]] of them, [[1:6|by which they have sinned against thee|quibus peccaverunt tibi]]: that is, I confess that they have sinned, that thou mayest deign to forgive them.

paras.t: Ego et domus, id est cognatio, patris mei peccavimus. Hoc addit, ne videatur se inaniter justificare. Certumque est, quod et ipse Nehemias a venialibus non fuit immunis. Vanitate seducti sumus. Omne enim peccatum est vanitas quædam. Et Proverbiorum ait Scriptura: Stultus illudit peccatum. Et qui peccat, errat atque seducitur, judicans male, saltem in particulari. Propter quod omnis peccans, dicitur esse ignorans. Unde et Salomon protestatur: Omnis viri via, recta in oculis ejus. Hinc per Jeremiam Dominus loquitur: Quid invenerunt patres vestri iniquitatis in me, quia ambulaverunt post vanitatem, et vani facti sunt? Insuper, omnia ista terrena, transitoria et caduca, dicuntur vana et vanitates, juxta illud Ecclesiastæ, Vanitas vanitatum, et omnia vanitas: quibus seducuntur iniqui, secundum illud Sapientis, Creaturæ factæ sunt in tentationem animæ hominum, et in muscipulam pedibus insipientium. Et non custodivimus mandatum tuum, id est præcepta tua Decalogi, quæ dicuntur moralia, et cærimonias, id est præcepta cærimonialia, et judicia tua, id est mandata judicialia.
paras.en: [[1:6|I and my father's house have sinned|Ego et domus, id est cognatio, patris mei peccavimus]] (*house*, that is, kindred). He adds this lest he seem to justify himself idly. And it is certain that Nehemias himself was not free of venial sins. [[1:7|We have been seduced by vanity|Vanitate seducti sumus]]. For every sin is a kind of vanity. And in Proverbs Scripture says: [[Prov 14:9|A fool will laugh at sin|Stultus illudit peccatum]]. And he who sins errs and is led astray, judging wrongly, at least in the particular case. For this reason everyone who sins is said to be ignorant. Hence Solomon too declares: Every man's way is right in his own eyes[[Prov 21:2||]]. Hence by Jeremias the Lord says: [[Jer 2:5|What iniquity have your fathers found in me|Quid invenerunt patres vestri iniquitatis in me]], [[Jer 2:5|and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?|quia ambulaverunt post vanitatem, et vani facti sunt?]] Moreover, all these earthly, passing and perishable things are called vain and vanities, according to that saying of Ecclesiastes, [[Eccles 1:2|vanity of vanities, and all is vanity|Vanitas vanitatum, et omnia vanitas]]: by which the wicked are led astray, according to that saying of the Wise man: The creatures are made [[Wis 14:11|a temptation to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the unwise|in tentationem animæ hominum, et in muscipulam pedibus insipientium]]. [[1:7|and have not kept thy commandments|Et non custodivimus mandatum tuum]], that is, thy precepts of the Decalogue, which are called moral, [[1:7|and ceremonies|et cærimonias]], that is, the ceremonial precepts, [[1:7|and judgments|et judicia tua]], that is, the judicial commands.

paras.t: Memento verbi, id est, per effectum ostende te memorem promissionis seu pacti, quod mandasti, id est insinuasti, Moysi servo tuo, et per eum promulgari jussisti, dicens: Quum transgressi fueritis, ita enormiter, ut ultra tolerari non possit: juxta illud Jeremiæ, Non poterat vos Dominus ultra portare propter malitiam studiorum vestrorum; ego disperdam vos peste, captivitate, gladio, fame: de quibus Dominus ait per Ezechielem, Mittam in eos quatuor judicia mea pessima; et si revertamini ad me, cum condigna contritione et emendatione, et congregabo vos. Istud locutus est Dominus in Deuteronomio. Obsecro, Domine, sit auris tua intendens ad orationem servorum tuorum, qui volunt timere nomen tuum, id est te ipsum, filiali timore: ita ut etsi nondum sint in caritate, nec filialiter timeant te, tamen misericorditer eos prævenias, obicemque gratiæ tollas de corde ipsorum, et tuum spiritualem amorem ac filialem timorem ipsis infundas; et dirige servum tuum hodie, id est me ipsum, in omnibus: specialiter ad proponendum convenienter regi meam petitionem; et da ei misericordiam ante virum hunc, id est, coram rege Artaxerxe da mihi gratiam, qua ei acceptus sim in mea postulatione, ita ut pie impleat eam. Ego enim eram pincerna regis: ideo habui ei me præsentare, et potui eum ad accitum meum accedere.
paras.en: [[1:8|Remember the word|Memento verbi]], that is, show by the effect that thou art mindful of the promise or covenant, [[1:8|that thou commandedst|quod mandasti]], that is, didst make known, [[1:8|to Moses thy servant|Moysi servo tuo]], and didst order to be published by him, [[1:8|saying|dicens]]: [[1:8|If you shall transgress|Quum transgressi fueritis]] so monstrously that you can no longer be borne, according to that saying of Jeremias, [[Jer 44:22|the Lord could no longer bear, because of the evil of your doings|Non poterat vos Dominus ultra portare propter malitiam studiorum vestrorum]], [[1:8|I will scatter you abroad|ego disperdam vos]] [Denis reads *disperdam*, “I will destroy”, for *dispergam*, “I will scatter”] by pestilence, captivity, sword and famine: of which the Lord says by Ezechiel, I will send upon them [[Ezech 14:21|my four grievous judgments|quatuor judicia mea pessima]]; [[1:9|But if you return to me|et si revertamini ad me]] with fitting contrition and amendment, [[1:9|I will gather you|et congregabo vos]]. This the Lord spoke in Deuteronomy[[Deut 30:3||]] [the margin's numerals are unreadable]. [[1:11|I beseech thee, O Lord, let thy ear be attentive|Obsecro, Domine, sit auris tua intendens]] [[1:11|to the prayer of thy servants who desire to fear thy name|ad orationem servorum tuorum, qui volunt timere nomen tuum]], that is, thyself, with filial fear: so that, even if they are not yet in charity and do not fear thee as sons, yet thou mayest go before them in mercy, and take away from their hearts the obstacle to grace, and pour into them thy spiritual love and filial fear; [[1:11|and direct thy servant this day|et dirige servum tuum hodie]], that is, myself, in all things, and especially in setting my petition fittingly before the king; [[1:11|and give him mercy before this man|et da ei misericordiam ante virum hunc]]: that is, give me favour before king Artaxerxes, by which I may be acceptable to him in my request, so that he may graciously fulfil it. [[1:11|For I was the king's cupbearer|Ego enim eram pincerna regis]]: therefore I had to present myself to him, and could approach him when I was called.

paras.t: Juxta mysticum sensum, per Judæos in angustiis constitutos, et ipsam Jerusalem construere cupientes, intelliguntur electi fideles, qui Ecclesiæ reformationem desiderant, et ejus ruinam deplangunt: qui ab invisibilibus hostibus atque a pravis hominibus multipliciter affliguntur. Per Nehemiam quoque designantur æmulatores legis divinæ, ac zelatores divinæ justitiæ: qui videntes se propriis viribus Ecclesiæ reformationem procurare non posse, per orationes, jejunia, lacrimas ad Deum confugiunt, quatenus ipse suam dignetur reformare Ecclesiam. Muri autem Ecclesiæ, sunt prælati, doctores et prædicatores, quorum est gregem dominicum circumvallare, custodire, munire: qui dum scandalose atque carnaliter conversantur, muri Jerusalem dissipantur; de quorum dejectione est maxime contristandum, et pro eorum erectione orandum. Portæ autem Jerusalem, sunt virtutes et merita, per quæ patet ingressus in triumphantem Ecclesiam: quæ igne concupiscentiæ et carnalis amoris, flammaque iracundiæ et vitiorum incendio comburuntur in eis qui corruunt.
paras.en: According to the mystical sense, by the Jews set in straits and longing to build Jerusalem itself are understood the elect faithful, who desire the reform of the Church and bewail her ruin, and who are afflicted in many ways by invisible enemies and by wicked men. By Nehemias are signified those who are jealous for the divine law and zealous for the divine justice: who, seeing that they cannot bring about the reform of the Church by their own strength, take refuge in God by prayers, fasts and tears, so that He may deign to reform His Church. The walls of the Church are the prelates, doctors and preachers, whose part it is to wall round, guard and fortify the Lord's flock: and when they live scandalously and carnally, the walls of Jerusalem are broken down; over whose overthrow there must be the greatest sorrow, and for whose raising up there must be prayer. The gates of Jerusalem are the virtues and merits through which entrance lies open into the Church triumphant: which in those who fall are burnt up by the fire of concupiscence and carnal love, by the flame of anger and the blaze of vices.

2.title: Expositio capituli secundi: Factum est autem in mense Nisan
2.title_en: Exposition of the second chapter: And it came to pass in the month of Nisan

paras.t: Nunc recitatur, qualiter Nehemias de licentia regis Jerusalem venerit.
paras.en: Now it is related how Nehemias came to Jerusalem with the king's leave.

paras.t: Factum est autem in mense Nisan: qui cum nostro Aprili concurrit, aut partim cum Martio; anno vicesimo Artaxerxis regis. Præcedenti capitulo dictum est, quod in mense Casleu, id est Decembri, vel secundum quosdam, Novembri, anno vicesimo Artaxerxis, Nehemias interrogavit de statu Jerusalem: quomodo ergo eodem anno in mense Nisan factum est, quod hic narratur, quum isti duo menses non veniant in eodem anno, ita quod Nisan sequatur mensem Casleu, sicut hic agitur de mense Nisan, qui fuit post Casleu? Ad quod quidam respondent, quod Nehemias hic loquitur secundum modum computationis Judæorum, dicentium, mundum esse creatum in mense Tisseri, correspondenti partim nostro Septembri, et partim Octobri: et quod ille sit simpliciter primus mensis anni, et Casleu tertius, Nisanque septimus, quamvis postea ex eventu, mensis Nisan vocatus sit primus mensis anni, quia in eo filii Israel educti sunt de Ægypto.
paras.en: [[2:1|And it came to pass in the month of Nisan|Factum est autem in mense Nisan]], which coincides with our April, or partly with March; [[2:1|in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king|anno vicesimo Artaxerxis regis]]. In the preceding chapter it was said that in the month of Casleu, that is, December, or according to some, November, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes, Nehemias asked about the state of Jerusalem[[2 Esd 1:1||]]: how then did what is told here happen in the month of Nisan of the same year, since these two months do not come in the same year in such a way that Nisan follows the month of Casleu, as here the month of Nisan is meant, which came after Casleu? To this some answer that Nehemias speaks here according to the Jews' way of reckoning, who say that the world was created in the month of Tisri, which corresponds partly to our September and partly to October: and that this is simply the first month of the year, Casleu the third, and Nisan the seventh, although afterwards, from what took place in it, the month of Nisan was called the first month of the year, because in it the children of Israel were brought out of Egypt[[Ex 12:2||]].

paras.t: Et levavi manum meam, et dedi regi vinum, id est, vasculum in quo fuit vinum ei porrexi; et eram quasi languidus ante faciem ejus, id est pallidus ex præviis jejuniis, orationibus, fletibus, vigiliis atque tristitiis.
paras.en: [[2:1|and I took up|Et levavi]] my hand, [[2:1|and gave it to the king|et dedi regi]] the wine, that is, I held out to him the cup in which the wine was; [[2:1|and I was as one languishing away before his face|et eram quasi languidus ante faciem ejus]], that is, pale from the fasts, prayers, weeping, watchings and sorrows that had gone before.

paras.t: Dixitque mihi rex, suspicans quod mali aliquid cogitarem in eum, quasi volens eum intoxicare, et ex timore deprehendendi de tanto facinore pallescens: Quare vultus tuus tristis est, id est, signa interioris mœroris ostendit, quum te ægrotum non videam? Non est hoc frustra, id est absque causa notabili; sed malum, nescio quid sit istud, quia cordium secreta certo et determinate cognoscere, vires excellit humanas, in corde tuo est. Nam interiora per exteriora quædam, præsertim ex dispositione vultus et oculorum, probabiliter et in generali noscuntur, juxta illud Ecclesiastici: Ex visu cognoscitur vir, et ab occursu faciei cognoscitur sensatus; amictus corporis, et risus dentium, et ingressus hominis, enuntiant de illo. Unde et in Proverbiorum libro fertur: Quomodo in aquis resplendent vultus prospicientium, sic corda hominum manifesta sunt prudentibus.
paras.en: [[2:2|And the king said to me|Dixitque mihi rex]], suspecting that I was plotting some evil against him, as if I meant to poison him, and was growing pale for fear of being caught in so great a crime: [[2:2|Why is thy countenance sad|Quare vultus tuus tristis est]], that is, why does it show signs of inward grief, [[2:2|seeing thou dost not appear to be sick|quum te ægrotum non videam]]? [[2:2|this is not without cause|Non est hoc frustra]], that is, without some notable cause; [[2:2|but some evil, I know not what|sed malum, nescio quid]] it is, since to know the secrets of hearts certainly and definitely surpasses human powers, [[2:2|is in thy heart|in corde tuo est]]. For inward things are known from certain outward things, above all from the bearing of the face and eyes, with probability and in general, according to that of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 19:26|A man is known by his look, and a wise man, when thou meetest him, is known by his countenance.|Ex visu cognoscitur vir, et ab occursu faciei cognoscitur sensatus]] [[Ecclus 19:27|The attire of the body, and the laughter of the teeth, and the gait of the man, shew what he is|amictus corporis, et risus dentium, et ingressus hominis, enuntiant de illo]]. Hence it is also said in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 27:19|As the faces of them that look therein, shine in the water, so the hearts of men are laid open to the wise.|Quomodo in aquis resplendent vultus prospicientium, sic corda hominum manifesta sunt prudentibus]]

paras.t: Et timui valde ac nimis, ne forte rex excusationi meæ non crederet, et suæ suspicioni nimium inhæreret, sicque forsan per pœnas extorqueret a me veritatem. Et dixi regi: Rex, in æternum vive. Quasi dicat: Vitam tuam cupio jugiter conservari et prosperari, atque post vitam hanc æternaliter felicitari. Quare non mœreat, id est, rationabiliter tristetur, vultus meus, quia civitas domus sepulcrorum patris mei deserta est, id est vastata, ita quod nunc pauci morantur in ea, respectu temporum quæ captivitatem nostram præcesserunt. Sed cur ait, Civitas domus sepulcrorum patris mei, et non potius, Civitas domus sepulcri patrum meorum, quum apud Judæos consueverint patres et filii in eodem sepulcro recondi? Et respondendum, quod plurale frequenter pro singulari ponitur, et econtra. Sicque per patrem intelligit suos progenitores. Et portæ ejus combustæ sunt igni.
paras.en: [[2:2|And I was seized with an exceeding great fear|Et timui valde ac nimis]], lest perhaps the king should not believe my excuse, and should hold too firmly to his suspicion, and so perhaps wring the truth from me by torments. [[2:3|And I said to the king: O king, live for ever|Et dixi regi: Rex, in æternum vive]]. As if to say: I desire thy life to be ever preserved and prospered, and after this life to be made happy for ever. [[2:3|why should not|Quare non]] [[2:3|be sorrowful|mœreat]], that is, be sad with reason, [[2:3|my countenance|vultus meus]], [[2:3|seeing the city of the place of the sepulchres of my fathers is desolate|quia civitas domus sepulcrorum patris mei deserta est]], that is, laid waste, so that few now dwell in it in comparison with the times that went before our captivity. But why does he say, The city of the house of the sepulchres of my father, and not rather, The city of the house of the sepulchre of my fathers [the Latin has *sepulcrorum patris mei*, "of the sepulchres of my father"; the Douay-Rheims renders it "of my fathers"], since among the Jews fathers and sons were wont to be laid in the same sepulchre? The answer is that the plural is often put for the singular, and the other way round. And so by *father* he means his forefathers. [[2:3|and the gates thereof are burnt with fire|Et portæ ejus combustæ sunt igni]].

paras.t: Et ait mihi rex, qui ex verbis prætactis consideravit, quod Nehemias optaret civitatis suæ reparationem: Pro qua re postulas? Et oravi Deum cæli, oratione interna ac brevi, ut dirigeret me in petendo, regemque inclinaret ad consentiendum, et dixi ad regem: Si videtur regi bonum: quasi dicat, Tuæ discretioni totum committo; et si placet servis tuis, id est septem consiliatoribus tuis tibi adstantibus, de quorum consilio omnia agis, juxta morem regum Persarum atque Medorum: ut dictum est super Esdram, et Esther primo habetur; rogo ut mittas me in Judæam, et ædificabo eam, scilicet urbem Jerusalem, complendo ejus reædificationem a Zorobabel inchoatam, et ab Esdra auctam, et postea minoratam.
paras.en: [[2:4|Then the king said to me|Et ait mihi rex]], who from the words just spoken saw that Nehemias wished for the repair of his city: [[2:4|For what dost thou make request? And I prayed to the God of heaven|Pro qua re postulas? Et oravi Deum cæli]], with a brief and inward prayer, that he would guide me in asking and incline the king to consent, [[2:5|And I said to the king: If it seem good to the king|et dixi ad regem: Si videtur regi bonum]]: as if to say, I leave it all to thy discretion; and if it please thy servants [Denis reads *servis tuis*, "thy servants", where the Vulgate has *servus tuus*, "thy servant" (a footnote of the edition gives that reading); the Douay-Rheims has "if thy servant hath found favour in thy sight"], that is, thy seven counsellors who stand by thee, by whose counsel thou doest all things, according to the custom of the kings of the Persians and Medes, as was said on Esdras[[1 Esd 7:14||]] and is found in the first chapter of Esther[[Esth 1:13||]][[Esth 1:14||]]; I ask [[2:5|that thou wouldst send me into Judea|ut mittas me in Judæam]], [[2:5|and I will build it|et ædificabo eam]], namely the city of Jerusalem, completing its rebuilding, begun by Zorobabel, advanced by Esdras, and afterwards diminished.

paras.t: Dixitque mihi rex et regina: Usque ad quod tempus erit iter tuum, et quando reverteris? id est, quamdiu quæris ibi manere? Ex quo patet, quod rex et regina non libenter caruerunt præsentia tam modesti et fidelis pincernæ. Porro quid ad hanc interrogationem responderit Nehemias, non scribitur hic: sed infra recitat Nehemias, se rediisse ad regem anno regni ejus tricesimo secundo: sicque absens fuit annis duodecim, quoniam anno regni ejus vicesimo abiit versus Judæam.
paras.en: [[2:6|And the king said to me, and the queen|Dixitque mihi rex et regina]]: [[2:6|For how long shall thy journey be, and when wilt thou return|Usque ad quod tempus erit iter tuum, et quando reverteris?]]? that is, how long dost thou seek to stay there? From this it is plain that the king and queen were loath to lose the presence of so modest and faithful a cupbearer. What Nehemias answered to this question is not written here; but further on Nehemias relates that he returned to the king in the thirty-second year of his reign[[2 Esd 13:6||]]: and so he was away twelve years, since he went off towards Judea in the twentieth year of his reign.

paras.t: Et placui ante vultum regis, et misit me. Et constitui ei tempus, et dixi ei: Si regi videtur bonum, epistolas det mihi ad duces regionis, quæ est trans flumen Euphraten, officiatos regis, ut transducant me, donec veniam in Judæam, id est, cum securitate me ducant usque ad loca inter Judæos reversos sita; et epistolam ad Asaph custodem saltus, id est silvæ regis, ut det mihi ligna, ut tegere possim portas templi, turres domus, id est, cooperire summitatem templi instar turris constructi, vel turris ædificandæ prope templum pro ejus munitione, et muri civitatis, id est, ad operiendum portas muri, seu turres in eo fiendas, et domum quam ingressus fuero, id est, etiam ad tegendum domum quam inhabitabo. Et dedit mihi rex juxta manum Dei mei bonam mecum, id est, fecit quæ petii, secundum quod Deus gratiose et favorabiliter adfuit mihi. Præterea Josephus addit, quod Nehemias a rege dimissus, cum principibus militum atque equitibus venit Babyloniam, et secum inde duxit multos Judæorum eum sponte sequentes.
paras.en: [[2:6|And it pleased the king|Et placui ante vultum regis]] [Denis reads *placui*, "I pleased before the king's face", for the Vulgate's *placuit*], [[2:6|and he sent me|et misit me]]. [[2:6|and I fixed him a time|Et constitui ei tempus]], and I said to him: [[2:7|If it seem good to the king, let him give me letters to the governors of the country|Si regi videtur bonum, epistolas det mihi ad duces regionis]], which is [[2:7|beyond the river|trans flumen]] Euphrates, the king's officers, [[2:7|that they convey me over, till I come into Judea|ut transducant me, donec veniam in Judæam]], that is, that they bring me in safety as far as the places where the returned Jews are settled; [[2:8|And a letter to Asaph the keeper of the|et epistolam ad Asaph custodem]] [[2:8|king's forest|saltus]], that is, the king's woodland, [[2:8|to give me timber|ut det mihi ligna]], [[2:8|that I may cover the gates|ut tegere possim portas]] of the temple, [[2:8|of the tower of the house|turres domus]], that is, to roof the top of the temple, built like a tower, or of a tower to be built near the temple for its defence, [[2:8|and the walls of the city|et muri civitatis]], that is, to cover the gates of the wall, or the towers to be made in it, [[2:8|and the house that I shall enter into|et domum quam ingressus fuero]], that is, also to roof the house which I shall live in. [[2:8|And the king gave me according to the good hand of my God with me|Et dedit mihi rex juxta manum Dei mei bonam mecum]], that is, he did what I asked, according as God was graciously and favourably with me. Josephus adds besides that Nehemias, dismissed by the king, came to Babylonia with the captains of soldiers and horsemen, and took with him from there many of the Jews who followed him of their own accord.

paras.t: Et veni ad duces regionis trans flumen, dedique eis epistolas regis. Miserat autem rex mecum principes militum et equites. Et audierunt Sanaballat et Tobias. Hi erant hostes Judæorum, et de adventu Nehemiæ dolebant.
paras.en: [[2:9|And I came to the governors of the country beyond the river, and gave them the king's letters. And the king had sent with me captains of soldiers, and horsemen.|Et veni ad duces regionis trans flumen, dedique eis epistolas regis. Miserat autem rex mecum principes militum et equites]] [[2:10|And Sanaballat|Sanaballat]] and [[2:10|Tobias|Tobias]] [[2:10|heard it|Et audierunt]]. These were enemies of the Jews, and grieved at the coming of Nehemias.

paras.t: Consequenter in textu describitur, qualiter Nehemias ad tempus suum celavit propositum, et circuivit, consideravitque urbem et muros destructos, qualiter possent aptius reparari. Nec est difficultas in littera; tamen aliqua tangam. Et jumentum non erat mecum, nisi animal cui sedebam, hoc est, ego solus equitavi, et qui mecum circuibant, pedites erant. Egressus sum ante frontem Draconis, id est locum sic nominatum. Non erat locus, id est via apta ad progrediendum, jumento cui sedebam, quia distorta erant itinera, et ruinæ fuerunt ibidem factæ.
paras.en: Next the text describes how Nehemias kept his purpose hidden for a time, and went round and viewed the city and the ruined walls, to see how they might best be repaired. Nor is there any difficulty in the letter; yet I shall touch on a few things. [[2:12|and there was no beast with me, but the beast that I rode upon|Et jumentum non erat mecum, nisi animal cui sedebam]], that is, I alone rode, and those who went round with me were on foot. [[2:13|And I went out|Egressus sum]] [[2:13|before the dragon fountain|ante frontem Draconis]] [the edition prints *frontem*, "the front", with a footnote giving *fontem*, "the fountain", as the Vulgate has], that is, the place so named. [[2:14|and there was no place|Non erat locus]], that is, no way fit for going on, [[2:14|for the beast on which I rode|jumento cui sedebam]], because the paths were twisted, and there had been ruins made there.

paras.t: Et indicavi eis manum Dei, quod esset bona mecum, id est adsistentiam et auxilium Dei prosperum mihi ab ipso concessum. Vobis autem Samaritanis adversariis nostris gentilibus atque idololatris, non est pars, id est communio neque hereditaria portio, et justitia, id est cultus sincerus veri Dei, et memoria in bono in Jerusalem: id est, omnino alieni estis a Deo et a fideli populo ejus et ab urbe Jerusalem ad divinum cultum electa.
paras.en: [[2:18|And I shewed them|Et indicavi eis]] [[2:18|how the hand of my God was good with me|manum Dei, quod esset bona mecum]], that is, the prosperous help and assistance of God granted me by him. [[2:20|but you|Vobis autem]] Samaritans, our adversaries, gentiles and idolaters, [[2:20|have no part|non est pars]], that is, no fellowship nor hereditary portion, [[2:20|nor justice|et justitia]], that is, the sincere worship of the true God, [[2:20|nor remembrance|et memoria]] for good [[2:20|in Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]]: that is, you are wholly strangers to God, and to his faithful people, and to the city of Jerusalem chosen for divine worship.

paras.t: Juxta tropologiam, prælatus cupiens reformare Ecclesiam, debet omnes ejus ruinas, deformitates et abusiones considerare, et qualiter possint ac debeant reformari, perpendere: sicque secreto suo ad tempus opportunum abscondito, debet sibi viros idoneos associare, ac suum propositum insinuare eisdem; et ipsos hortari, ut sibi cooperentur et adsistant ad reformandum collapsa, et ut confidant in Domino, certi de adjutorio ejus, dummodo quod in ipsis est, fecerint, et ne timeant adversarios boni communis; imo parati sint pro Deo, pro æquitate, pro proximorum salute, et pro bono communi persecutiones pati ac mortem subire.
paras.en: According to the tropology [that is, the moral sense], a prelate who wishes to reform the Church ought to view all its ruins, deformities and abuses, and weigh how they can and ought to be reformed: and so, keeping his secret hidden until the fitting time, he ought to join to himself suitable men and make his purpose known to them; and exhort them to work with him and help him in restoring what has fallen, and to trust in the Lord, sure of his help, provided they do what is in their power, and not to fear the adversaries of the common good; nay, to be ready to suffer persecution and to undergo death for God, for justice, for the salvation of their neighbours, and for the common good.

3.title: Expositio capituli tertii: Et surrexit Eliasib sacerdos magnus
3.title_en: Exposition of the third chapter: Then Eliasib the high priest arose

paras.t: Hic ipsa reædificatio civitatis Jerusalem et murorum ac portarum ejus describitur.
paras.en: Here the rebuilding itself of the city of Jerusalem, and of its walls and gates, is described.

paras.t: Et surrexit Eliasib sacerdos magnus, id est pontifex Judæorum: qui, secundum Josephum et Magistrum in historiis, fuit filius Joachim seu Eliachim pontificis, qui Joachim erat filius Josue filii Josedec. Et fratres ejus sacerdotes, et ædificaverunt portam Gregis. Alia translatio continet: Ædificaverunt portam et Probaticam piscinam. Fuitque porta hæc juxta templum: per quam inducebantur greges animalium offerendorum. De piscina autem Probatica habetur apud Joannem. De hac porta quidam exponunt illud Michææ: Et tu, turris Gregis nebulosa. Tamen sicut ibi exposui, per turrim illam intelligitur ibi ad litteram templum. Denique in hac ædificatione decuit principem sacerdotum cum suis exsistere primum, et portam construere prope templum. Ipsi sanctificaverunt, id est, firmiter statuerunt ea, ad Dei honorem: nam sanctum uno modo idem est quod firmum; et statuerunt valvas ejus, id est portas ejus seu januas: quæ a volvendo nomen sortitæ sunt, quia in apertione et clausura volvuntur ac revolvuntur, et per portas cointelliguntur vectes et seræ; et usque ad turrim centum cubitorum sanctificaverunt eam, id est firmaverunt, ædificando juxta eam in muro usque ad turrim centum cubitorum ab una parte, et usque ad turrim Hananeel, ex alia parte. Unde prædictum fuit a Jeremia: Ædificabitur civitas Domino a turre Hananeel. Et juxta eum, id est prope ædificata a pontifice, ædificaverunt viri Jericho, hoc est oriundi ex urbe sic dicta; et juxta eum, forsan ex alio latere, ædificavit Zachur filius Amri, incipiendo ubi dimisit Eliasib.
paras.en: [[3:1|Then Eliasib the high priest arose|Et surrexit Eliasib sacerdos magnus]], that is, the pontiff of the Jews, who according to Josephus and the Master in the Histories was the son of Joachim, or Eliachim, the pontiff, which Joachim was the son of Josue the son of Josedec. [[3:1|and his brethren the priests|Et fratres ejus sacerdotes]], [[3:1|and they built the flock gate|et ædificaverunt portam Gregis]]. Another translation has: They built the gate and the Probatic pool. This gate was next to the temple, and through it were brought in the flocks of animals to be offered. Of the Probatic pool we have it in John[[John 5:2||]]. Some explain of this gate that saying of Micheas: [[Mich 4:8|And thou, O cloudy tower of the flock|Et tu, turris Gregis nebulosa]]. Yet, as I explained there, by that tower the temple is meant there literally. Moreover, in this building it was fitting that the prince of the priests with his own should be the first, and should build the gate near the temple. [[3:1|they sanctified it|Ipsi sanctificaverunt]], that is, they set them up firmly to the honour of God: for *holy* in one sense is the same as *firm*; [[3:1|and set up the doors thereof|et statuerunt valvas ejus]], that is, its gates or doors, which got their name from turning [*valvæ*, as if from *volvere*, “to turn”], because in opening and shutting they turn and turn back; and with the doors are understood the bars and bolts; [[3:1|even unto the tower of a hundred cubits they sanctified it|et usque ad turrim centum cubitorum sanctificaverunt eam]], that is, strengthened it, building next to it in the wall as far as the tower of a hundred cubits on one side, [[3:1|unto the tower of Hananeel|et usque ad turrim Hananeel]] on the other side. Hence it was foretold by Jeremias: [[Jer 31:38|the city shall be built to the Lord from the tower of Hanameel|Ædificabitur civitas Domino a turre Hananeel]]. [[3:2|And next to him|Et juxta eum, id est]], that is, near what was built by the pontiff, [[3:2|the men of Jericho built|ædificaverunt viri Jericho]], that is, men born in the city so called; [[3:2|and next to them|et juxta eum, forsan]] [[3:2|built Zachur the son of Amri|ædificavit Zachur filius Amri]], perhaps on the other side, beginning where Eliasib left off.

paras.t: Portam autem Piscium, sic vocatam quia per eam copia piscium inferebatur, ædificaverunt filii Asnaa. Et ipsi texuerunt, id est construxerunt; vel, texerunt, id est operuerunt ex lignis, ut et murus fortius cohæreret. Hæc porta, secundum Josephum, appellata est postea porta David, quoniam fuit ex opposito montis Sion, id est illius partis Jerusalem: quæ pars vocata est civitas David, ut patet secundo libro Regum.
paras.en: [[3:3|But the fish gate|Portam autem Piscium]], so called because plenty of fish was brought in by it, [[3:3|the sons of Asnaa built|ædificaverunt filii Asnaa]]. [[3:3|they covered it|Et ipsi texuerunt]], that is, they built it [*texuerunt*, “they wove”, that is, put it together]; or *texerunt*, that is, they covered it over with timber, so that the wall too might hold together more strongly [the OCR is unclear between the two readings]. This gate, according to Josephus, was afterwards called the gate of David, since it was opposite mount Sion, that is, opposite that part of Jerusalem which was called the city of David, as is plain in the second book of Kings[[2 Kings 5:7||]][[2 Kings 5:9||]].

paras.t: Et juxta eos ædificaverunt Thecueni, id est nati ex urbe Thecua: de qua fuit Amos propheta, et mulier sapiens quam Joab misit ad David, prout secundo libro Regum describitur. Optimates autem, id est superiores, eorum, non supposuerunt colla sua in opere Domini, id est, non adjuverunt in ædificiis istis: in quo eorum negligentia et vulgarium diligentia denotantur.
paras.en: [[3:5|And next to them the Thecuites built|Et juxta eos ædificaverunt Thecueni]], that is, men born in the city of Thecua: from which came Amos the prophet[[Amos 1:1||]], and the wise woman whom Joab sent to David, as is described in the second book of Kings[[2 Kings 14:2||]]. [[3:5|but their great men|Optimates autem]], that is, their superiors, [[3:5|did not put their necks to the work of their Lord|non supposuerunt colla sua in opere Domini]], that is, did not help in these buildings: in which their negligence and the diligence of the common people are pointed out.

paras.t: Et portam Veterem ædificaverunt Joiada filius Phasea, et Mosollam filius Besodia. Hæc porta vocata est vetus, quia vestigia ejus apparuerunt a diebus Jebusæorum atque Melchisedech, ut in Scholastica fertur historia. Juxta eos ædificavit Meltias; et Maspha: quod est hic nomen viri, qui erat pro duce in regione trans flumen, id est, vices ducis illius supplevit: quia ut dicitur, dux quidam trans flumen, quamvis gentilis natione, cupiebat ad ædificandum contribuere ex devotione: quod fecit per virum prædictum. Et dimiserunt Jerusalem, extra eam ædificando, vel eam extendendo.
paras.en: [[3:6|And Joiada the son of Phasea, and Mosollam the son of Besodia built the old gate|Et portam Veterem ædificaverunt Joiada filius Phasea, et Mosollam filius Besodia]]. This gate was called old because its traces appeared from the days of the Jebusites and of Melchisedech, as is related in the Scholastic History. [[3:7|And next to them built Meltias|Juxta eos ædificavit Meltias]]; [[3:7|and Maspha|et Maspha]], which is here the name of a man, [[3:7|for the governor that was in the country beyond the river|qui erat pro duce in regione trans flumen]], that is, he took the place of that governor: for, as is said, a certain governor beyond the river, though a gentile by nation, desired out of devotion to contribute to the building, which he did through the aforesaid man. [[3:8|and they left Jerusalem|Et dimiserunt Jerusalem]], by building outside it, or by extending it.

paras.t: Et portam Vallis, per quam ibatur de civitate ad vallem Josaphat, ædificavit Hanun. Et portam Sterquilinii, per quam tempore pluvioso immunditiæ civitatis decurrebant in torrentem Cedron. Portam Fontis, quæ et infra porta Aquarum vocatur, et a fonte sibi propinquo sic dicta est, ædificavit Sellum. Nempe portæ hic nominatæ, inveniuntur et alia nomina habere. Princeps pagi, id est villæ seu vici Maspha; et muros piscinæ Siloe in hortum regis, id est, muros piscinæ sic nuncupatæ construxit usque ad hortum regis; vel ædificavit muros piscinæ fluentis versus regis hortum. Dicit autem Isaias: Aquæ Siloe transeunt cum silentio. Apud Joannem quoque Evangelistam dicitur: Vade, lava in natatoria Siloe, quod interpretatur missus. Et usque ad gradus qui descendunt de civitate David. Siquidem ad civitatem David, hoc est ad arcem Sion, ascendebatur per gradus.
paras.en: [[3:13|And the gate of the valley|Et portam Vallis]], by which one went out of the city to the valley of Josaphat, [[3:13|Hanun built|ædificavit Hanun]]. [[3:14|And the gate of the dunghill|Et portam Sterquilinii]], through which in rainy weather the filth of the city ran down into the torrent Cedron. [[3:15|And the gate of the fountain|Portam Fontis]], which further on is also called the water gate[[2 Esd 8:1||]], and is so named from a fountain near it, [[3:15|Sellum|ædificavit Sellum]] built. For the gates named here are found to have other names as well. [[3:15|lord of the street of Maspha|princeps pagi Maspha]], that is, of the village or quarter of Maspha; [[3:15|and the walls of the pool of Siloe|et muros piscinæ Siloe]] [[3:15|unto the king's guard|in hortum regis]] [*in hortum regis*, “to the king's garden”; the Douay-Rheims has “guard”], that is, he built the walls of the pool so named as far as the king's garden; or he built the walls of the pool that flows towards the king's garden. Now Isaias speaks of [[Is 8:6|the waters of Siloe, that go with silence|Aquæ Siloe transeunt cum silentio]]. And in John the Evangelist it is said: [[John 9:7|Go, wash in the pool of Siloe, which is interpreted, Sent|Vade, lava in natatoria Siloe, quod interpretatur missus]]. [[3:15|and unto the steps that go down from the city of David|Et usque ad gradus qui descendunt de civitate David]]. For one went up by steps to the city of David, that is, to the citadel of Sion[[2 Esd 12:36||]].

paras.t: Post eum ædificavit Nehemias filius Azboc, usque contra sepulcrum, id est ex opposito sepulcri, David regis, qui sepultus est in civitate David, ut legitur tertio Regum libro, et usque ad domum fortium, in qua fortes regis David seu agonistæ solebant manere: non quod domus illa adhuc stetit, sed usque ad locum ubi aliquando stabat, porrigebatur ædificatio hujus.
paras.en: [[3:16|After him built Nehemiah the son of Azboc|Post eum ædificavit Nehemias filius Azboc]], [[3:16|as far as over against the sepulchre|usque contra sepulcrum]], that is, opposite the sepulchre, [[3:16|of David|David]] the king, who was buried in the city of David, as we read in the third book of Kings[[3 Kings 2:10||]], [[3:16|and to the house of the mighty|et usque ad domum fortium]], in which king David's mighty men or champions used to stay: not that that house was still standing, but this man's building reached as far as the place where it once stood.

paras.t: Nathinæi autem, qui ligna et aquas comportabant ad domum Dei, habitabant in Ophel, id est loco sic dicto, non remote a templo. Sursum autem a porta Equorum ædificaverunt sacerdotes. Hæc porta non fuit porta civitatis, sed posita erat ante atria templi: usque ad quam licuit equitando ascendere versus templum, atque exinde dicitur incepisse habitatio sacerdotum. Littera plana est.
paras.en: [[3:26|And the Nathinites|Nathinæi autem]], who carried wood and water to the house of God, [[3:26|dwelt in Ophel|habitabant in Ophel]], that is, in a place so called, not far from the temple. [[3:28|And upward from the horse gate the priests built|Sursum autem a porta Equorum ædificaverunt sacerdotes]]. This gate was not a gate of the city, but stood before the courts of the temple: up to it one might ride towards the temple, and from there the dwelling of the priests is said to have begun. The letter is plain.

paras.t: Mystice potest hoc loco per Nehemiam Christus intelligi, qui militantem ædificavit Ecclesiam. Cujus cooperatores fuerunt gloriosi Apostoli, ceterique discipuli ac prælati, prædicatores atque doctores: quorum quisque domum seu congregationem sibi commissam ædificavit exemplo et documentis. Porro, per septem portas, puta per sex portas civitatis, et per portam Equorum, rite intelliguntur septem ecclesiastica sacramenta, per quæ ad cæleste regnum pertingitur, vel septem dona Spiritus Sancti, seu tres virtutes theologicæ et quatuor cardinales. Specialiter demum, per portam Gregis, designatur spontanea resignatio sui ipsius, et mortificatio propriæ voluntatis, seu crucifixio propriæ carnis cum vitiis et concupiscentiis: per quæ omnia offert se homo suo Creatori, sicut per portam Gregis inducebantur pecora immolatitia Domino offerenda. Per portam Piscium, figurata est prædicatio Evangelii, per quam homines quasi pisces capti, Christo incorporantur, qui dixit ad summum Apostolum: Ex hoc jam homines eris capiens. Per portam Veterem, intelligitur cognitio Scripturarum veteris Testamenti, per quam fides corroboratur. Per portam Fontis, effusio lacrimarum desiderio regni cælestis, seu copia gratiarum, vel aqua sapientiæ salutaris. Per portam Vallis, sancta humilitas. Per portam Sterquilinii, recognitio propriæ defectuositatis et expurgatio vitiorum. Per portam Equorum, fortitudo, fervor, velocitas prædicatorum ac prælatorum, quorum est Christum undique circumferre.
paras.en: Mystically, Nehemias can in this place be understood as Christ, who built the Church militant. His fellow workers were the glorious Apostles, and the other disciples and prelates, preachers and doctors: each of whom built the house or congregation entrusted to him by example and teaching. Further, by the seven gates, namely the six gates of the city and the horse gate, are fitly understood the seven sacraments of the Church, by which the heavenly kingdom is reached; or the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]]; or the three theological virtues and the four cardinal ones. In particular, by the flock gate is signified the willing surrender of oneself and the mortification of one's own will, or the crucifying of one's own flesh with its vices and concupiscences[[Gal 5:24||]]: by all of which a man offers himself to his Creator, as by the flock gate the beasts for sacrifice were brought in to be offered to the Lord. By the fish gate is figured the preaching of the Gospel, by which men, caught as it were like fish, are incorporated into Christ, who said to the chief Apostle: [[Luke 5:10|from henceforth thou shalt catch men|Ex hoc jam homines eris capiens]]. By the old gate is understood the knowledge of the Scriptures of the Old Testament, by which faith is strengthened. By the gate of the fountain, the shedding of tears from desire of the heavenly kingdom, or abundance of graces, or [[Ecclus 15:3|the water of wholesome wisdom|aqua sapientiæ salutaris]]. By the gate of the valley, holy humility. By the gate of the dunghill, the acknowledgement of one's own failings and the purging away of vices. By the horse gate, the strength, fervour and swiftness of preachers and prelates, whose part it is to carry Christ about everywhere.

paras.t: Postremo, per optimates Thecuenorum non supponentes colla sua in opere Dei, recte intelliguntur, qui in Ecclesia fulgent ecclesiastica dignitate, sed per negligentiam torpent, et carnali conversatione læduntur: qui pulchra dicunt magnaque prædicant, sed ea non exsequuntur. De quibus ait Salvator: Alligant onera gravia et importabilia, et imponunt ea super humeros hominum, digito autem suo nolunt ea movere. Similiter nobiles et potentes, quum dicat Apostolus: Quia non multi potentes, non multi nobiles sunt inter vos; sed abjecta mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat fortia. Nam et teste Gregorio: Hos elegit Deus quos despicit mundus. De quibus ait Psalmista: In labore hominum non sunt, et cum hominibus non flagellabuntur; ideo tenuit eos superbia.
paras.en: Lastly, by the great men of the Thecuites who did not put their necks to the work of God are rightly understood those who shine in the Church with ecclesiastical dignity, but grow sluggish through negligence and are harmed by carnal living: who say fine things and preach great things, but do not carry them out. Of whom the Saviour says: [[Matt 23:4|For they bind heavy and insupportable burdens and lay them on men's shoulders: but with a finger of their own they will not move them.|Alligant onera gravia et importabilia, et imponunt ea super humeros hominum, digito autem suo nolunt ea movere]] Likewise the noble and mighty, since the Apostle says that there are [[1 Cor 1:26|not many mighty, not many noble|non multi potentes, non multi nobiles]] among you; but the base things of the world God has chosen, [[1 Cor 1:27|that he may confound the strong|ut confundat fortia]]. For, as Gregory testifies, “God has chosen those whom the world despises.” Of whom the Psalmist says: [[Ps 72:5|They are not in the labour of men: neither shall they be scourged like other men|In labore hominum non sunt, et cum hominibus non flagellabuntur]]; [[Ps 72:6|Therefore pride hath held them fast|ideo tenuit eos superbia]].

4.title: Expositio capituli quarti: Factum est autem quum audisset Sanaballat
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: And it came to pass, that when Sanaballat heard

paras.t: Ponitur hic unum obstaculorum, quo adversarii Judæorum conati sunt Judæos ab ædificatione retrahere, utpote eos acriter impugnando.
paras.en: Here is set down one of the obstacles by which the adversaries of the Jews tried to draw the Jews back from the building, namely by fiercely attacking them.

paras.t: Factum est autem quum audisset Sanaballat inter Samaritanos præcipuus, quod ædificaremus murum, iratus est valde, invidens prosperitati ædificantium, et dixit: Quid Judæi faciunt imbecilles, id est infirmi? quasi dicat: Non poterunt facere aliquid magni. Num dimittent eos gentes? id est, gentiles in eorum circuitu commorantes, non permittent eos opus inchoatum complere. Sed et Tobias Ammonites proximus ejus, ait: Ædificent, id est, non est curandum de ædificatione ipsorum. Si ascenderit vulpes, transiliet murum eorum lapideum, tam bassus et debilis erit murus quem faciunt: et sic poterimus murum illum ad placitum dissipare.
paras.en: [[4:1|And it came to pass, that when Sanaballat heard|Factum est autem quum audisset Sanaballat]], the chief among the Samaritans, [[4:1|that we were building the wall he was angry|quod ædificaremus murum, iratus est valde]], envying the prosperity of the builders, [[4:2|And said|et dixit]]: [[4:2|What are the silly Jews doing|Quid Judæi faciunt imbecilles]], that is, the weak Jews? as if to say: They will not be able to do anything great. [[4:2|Will the Gentiles let them alone|Num dimittent eos gentes]]? that is, the gentiles living round about them will not allow them to finish the work they have begun. [[4:3|Tobias also the Ammonite who was by him said: Let them build|Sed et Tobias Ammonites proximus ejus, ait: Ædificent]], that is, there is no need to trouble about their building. [[4:3|if a fox go up, he will leap over their stone wall|Si ascenderit vulpes, transiliet murum eorum lapideum]], so low and weak will the wall be that they are making: and so we shall be able to pull that wall down as we please.

paras.t: Et dixit Nehemias. Hoc non est de textu. Audi, Deus noster, quia facti sumus despectui, id est, injuste nos contempserunt. Converte opprobrium super caput eorum, id est, pro eorum opprobrio quo nos aspernati sunt, puniantur a te; et da eos in despectionem in terra captivitatis, id est, pro eo quod nos spreverunt injuste, nec compassi sunt reversis a captivitate, fac eos juste contemni et captivari. Ne operias iniquitatem eorum, id est, inultam non deseras, et peccata eorum coram facie tua non deleantur, id est, non tradantur oblivioni a te, donec debite castigentur: quia irriserunt ædificantes urbem cultus divini et templum Dei.
paras.en: And Nehemias said (this is not part of the text): [[4:4|Hear thou our God, for we are despised|Audi, Deus noster, quia facti sumus despectui]], that is, they have despised us unjustly. [[4:4|turn their reproach upon their own head|Converte opprobrium super caput eorum]], that is, for the reproach with which they have scorned us, let them be punished by thee; [[4:4|and give them to be despised in a land of captivity|et da eos in despectionem in terra captivitatis]], that is, because they despised us unjustly and had no pity on those returned from captivity, make them justly despised and taken captive. [[4:5|Cover not their iniquity|Ne operias iniquitatem eorum]], that is, do not leave it unavenged, [[4:5|and let not their sin be blotted out from before thy face|et peccata eorum coram facie tua non deleantur]], that is, let them not be forgotten by thee until they are duly chastised: [[4:5|because they have mocked thy builders|quia irriserunt ædificantes]] of the city of divine worship and of the temple of God.

paras.t: Non ex odio, sed potius zelo justitiæ, oravit hæc Nehemias, et ut in præsenti purgarentur et castigarentur. Vel quasi prophetice loquens hæc protulit. Sic enim et in libro Psalmorum multa dicuntur, ut est: Redde vicinis nostris septuplum in sinu eorum, improperium ipsorum quod exprobraverunt tibi, Domine. Et Jeremias: Induc (inquit) super eos diem afflictionis, et duplici contritione contere eos. Hi autem erant infideles, et obstinati in vitiis, ac publici hostes veræ religionis ac boni communis: ideo licuit contra eos sic exorare, non odiendo naturam neque personam secundum se, sed impietatem et impios secundum quod tales.
paras.en: Nehemias prayed thus not out of hatred, but rather out of zeal for justice, and that they might be purged and chastised in the present life. Or he uttered these things speaking, as it were, prophetically. For so too many things are said in the book of Psalms, as: [[Ps 78:12|And render to our neighbours sevenfold in their bosom: the reproach wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord|Redde vicinis nostris septuplum in sinu eorum, improperium ipsorum quod exprobraverunt tibi, Domine]]. And Jeremias: [[Jer 17:18|bring|Induc]], he says, [[Jer 17:18|upon them the day of affliction, and with a double destruction, destroy them|super eos diem afflictionis, et duplici contritione contere eos]]. Now these men were unbelievers, obstinate in vices, and public enemies of the true religion and of the common good: so it was lawful to pray thus against them, not hating their nature, nor their person as such, but impiety, and the impious as such.

paras.t: Factum est autem, quum audissent quod obducta esset cicatrix muri Jerusalem, et cœpissent interrupta concludi, id est, interruptio muri esset reparata in rimulis et scissuris, irati sunt nimis, et congregati sunt omnes ut venirent pariter ad expugnandum nos. Et oravimus Deum, sine cujus auxilio non potuissemus illis prævalere, et posuimus custodes super murum.
paras.en: [[4:7|And it came to pass|Factum est autem]], when they [[4:7|heard that the walls of Jerusalem were made up, and the breaches began to be closed|quod obducta esset cicatrix muri Jerusalem, et cœpissent interrupta concludi]], that is, that the breach in the wall had been repaired in its cracks and rents, [[4:7|they were exceedingly angry|irati sunt nimis]], [[4:8|And they all assembled themselves together, to come|Et congregati sunt omnes ut venirent]] together to fight against us. [[4:9|And we prayed to|Et oravimus]] God, without whose help we could not have prevailed over them, [[4:9|and set watchmen upon the wall|et posuimus custodes super murum]].

paras.t: Dixit autem Judas, id est tribus seu populus Juda, aut aliquis vir notabilis Judas nomine: Debilitata est fortitudo portantis, id est, portantes onera sunt lassati, et humus nimia est, hoc est, terra efferenda, ut convenientius fiant ædificia, est copiosa, ita ut laboriosum sit eam efferre. Nec apta est expositio, ut per terram intelligantur calx et arena: quæ propriis poterant nominibus designari. Et nos non poterimus ædificare, propter hæc impedimenta. Isti cœperunt animo frangi, pusillanimitateque dejici.
paras.en: [[4:10|And Juda said|Dixit autem Judas]], that is, the tribe or people of Juda, or some notable man named Judas: [[4:10|The strength of the bearer of burdens is decayed|Debilitata est fortitudo portantis]], that is, those carrying burdens are worn out, [[4:10|and the rubbish is very much|et humus nimia est]], that is, the earth to be carried out, so that the buildings may be made more fitly, is plentiful, so that it is toilsome to carry it out. Nor is it a fitting exposition that by the earth lime and sand are meant, which could have been signified by their own names. [[4:10|and we shall not be able to build|Et nos non poterimus ædificare]], because of these hindrances. These men began to be broken in spirit and cast down by faintheartedness.

paras.t: Et dixerunt hostes nostri: Nesciant, donec veniamus in medium eorum, id est, improvise irruamus in ædificantes. Factum est autem venientibus Judæis qui habitabant juxta eos, id est prope Samaritanos, qui avisabant Nehemiam et suos de adversariorum confœderatione et proposito veniendi contra ipsum et populum suum, statui post murum populum in ordine cum gladiis suis et lanceis, id est in acie ordinata ad standum extra civitatem, ut se opponerent hostibus. Et surrexi, et aio ad optimates: Nolite timere a facie eorum. Quum audissent inimici nostri nuntiatum esse nobis de eorum insidiis et adventu, dissipavit Deus consilium eorum, ingerendo eis timorem seu dissensionem.
paras.en: [[4:11|And our enemies said: Let them not know|Et dixerunt hostes nostri: Nesciant]], [[4:11|till we come in the midst of them|donec veniamus in medium eorum]], that is, let us fall upon the builders unawares. [[4:12|And it came to pass, that when the Jews that dwelt by them came|Factum est autem venientibus Judæis qui habitabant juxta eos]], that is, near the Samaritans, who warned Nehemias and his men of the adversaries' league and of their purpose of coming against him and his people, I [[4:13|set the people|statui post murum populum]] [[4:13|in order, with their swords, and spears|in ordine cum gladiis suis et lanceis]] behind the wall, that is, in battle array, to stand outside the city and oppose the enemy. [[4:14|and rose up: and I said to the chief men|Et surrexi, et aio ad optimates]]: [[4:14|be not afraid of them|Nolite timere a facie eorum]]. When [[4:15|our enemies heard that the thing had been told us|inimici nostri nuntiatum esse nobis]] of their ambush and coming, [[4:15|God defeated their counsel|dissipavit Deus consilium eorum]], putting fear or discord into them.

paras.t: A die illa media pars juvenum eorum, id est prædictorum bellatorum nostrorum, faciebat opus in muro, et media pars parata erat ad bellum, vacans ab opere, ut esset fortis et præcincta ad pugnam, et principes post eos, ad dirigendum juvenes circa pugnam. Et dixi ad optimates et reliquam partem vulgi: Deus pugnabit pro nobis, nos confortando, et adversarios prosternendo.
paras.en: [[4:16|from that day forward|A die illa]] [[4:16|half of their young men|media pars juvenum eorum]], that is, of our warriors aforesaid, [[4:16|did the work|faciebat opus]] on the wall, [[4:16|and half were ready for to fight|et media pars parata erat ad bellum]], free from the work, so as to be strong and girded for battle, [[4:16|and the rulers were behind them|et principes post eos]], to direct the young men in the fighting. [[4:19|And I said to the nobles|Et dixi ad optimates]] [[4:19|and to the rest of the common people|et reliquam partem vulgi]]: [[4:20|our God will fight for us|Deus pugnabit pro nobis]], strengthening us and laying our adversaries low.

paras.t: Et dixi populo: Unusquisque cum puero suo, id est ministro aut filio, maneat in medio Jerusalem tanquam in loco magis munito, et ubi magis necessaria sunt auxilia contra hostes, et sint vobis vices, id est vicissitudines seu alternationes, per diem et noctem ad operandum, ut scilicet una parte operante et vigilante, alia paulisper repauset. Ego autem et fratres, id est cognati, mei et pueri mei et custodes, non deponebamus vestimenta nostra de nocte, quia modicissimo somno eramus contenti. Unusquisque tantum nudabatur ad baptismum, id est, solum nudavit se ad aliquantulam horam, ut juxta morem et ritum legis lavaret, et lavando purificaret se, vel corpus suum a sudoribus immunditiisque ex labore contractis lavando mundaret.
paras.en: And [[4:22|I said to the people|dixi populo]]: [[4:22|Let every one with his servant|Unusquisque cum puero suo]], that is, his attendant or son, [[4:22|stay in the midst of Jerusalem|maneat in medio Jerusalem]], as in the better fortified place, and where help against the enemy is most needed, [[4:22|and let us take our turns|et sint vobis vices]] [Denis reads *vobis*, "to you", for the Vulgate's *nobis*], that is, changes or alternations, [[4:22|in the night, and by day, to work|per diem et noctem ad operandum]], so that, while one part works and keeps watch, the other may rest a little. [[4:23|Now I and my brethren|Ego autem et fratres]], that is, my kinsmen, [[4:23|and my servants, and the watchmen|mei et pueri mei et custodes]], [[4:23|did not put off our clothes|non deponebamus vestimenta nostra]] by night, for we were content with the very least sleep. [[4:23|only every man stripped himself when he was to be washed|Unusquisque tantum nudabatur ad baptismum]] [*ad baptismum*, literally "for the washing"], that is, each stripped himself only for a short while, to wash according to the custom and rite of the law, and by washing to purify himself, or to cleanse his body by washing from the sweat and dirt gathered from the work.

paras.t: Spiritualiter, per adversarios Judæorum præfatos, intelliguntur hæretici et perversi, persecutores et tyranni, qui profectui et reformationi adversantur Ecclesiæ: contra quos, sæculares fideles corporalibus armis armantur, et etiam divini invocatione subsidii; spirituales autem personæ, orationibus pugnant et lacrimis. Omnes quoque ædificantes et bonum Ecclesiæ promoventes, accincti sunt gladio spiritus, quod est verbum Dei, ac veræ discretionis judicio. Et sicut Nehemias ac sui, propter nullam adversantium improbitatem, ab incepto opere cessaverunt, ita debemus in sanctis actibus esse constantes.
paras.en: Spiritually, by the aforesaid adversaries of the Jews are understood heretics and wicked men, persecutors and tyrants, who oppose the progress and reform of the Church: against whom the faithful of the world are armed with bodily weapons, and also with calling on God's help; while spiritual persons fight with prayers and tears. And all who build and further the good of the Church are girded with the [[Eph 6:17|sword of the Spirit (which is the word of God)|gladio spiritus, quod est verbum Dei]], and with the judgement of true discretion. And as Nehemias and his men did not cease from the work they had begun for any wickedness of their adversaries, so ought we to be constant in holy deeds.

5.title: Expositio capituli quinti: Et factus est clamor populi
5.title_en: Exposition of the fifth chapter: Now there was a great cry of the people

paras.t: Reprehenduntur hic ditiores Judæorum de avaritia, immisericordia, et usura circa proximos suos extenuatos Judæos.
paras.en: Here the richer of the Jews are rebuked for avarice, lack of mercy, and usury towards their neighbours, the impoverished Jews.

paras.t: Et factus est clamor populi et uxorum ejus magnus, id est, mediocres pauperesque Judæi et eorum uxores, querulose et miserabiliter clamaverunt, adversus fratres, id est cognatos, suos Judæos divites et potentes, a quibus gravabantur usuris: ita quod divites contra legem mutuaverunt pauperibus sub usura, imo filios ac filias indigentium Judæorum emerunt in servos et ancillas: quod et pauperes aliqui necessitate quadam compulsi, adhuc sponte pati proposuerunt, sicut subjungitur.
paras.en: [[5:1|Now there was a great cry of the people, and of their wives|Et factus est clamor populi et uxorum ejus magnus]], that is, the Jews of the middling and poorer sort and their wives cried out plaintively and piteously, [[5:1|against their brethren|adversus fratres]], that is, their kinsmen, [[5:1|the Jews|suos Judæos]] who were rich and powerful, by whom they were burdened with usuries: so that the rich, against the law, lent to the poor at usury[[Ex 22:25||]][[Lev 25:36||]][[Lev 25:37||]], nay, bought the sons and daughters of needy Jews as menservants and maidservants[[Lev 25:39||]] [the margin gives Exod. xxii, 25; Lev. xxv, 36, 37, 39–46]: which some of the poor, driven by a kind of necessity, proposed to suffer still of their own accord, as is added.

paras.t: Et erant qui dicerent: Filii nostri et filiæ nostræ multæ sunt nimis: ita quod eos alere non valemus; accipiamus pro pretio eorum frumentum, et comedamus et vivamus, id est, vendamus eos divitibus, atque pro pretio accipiamus victualia. Et erant qui dicerent: Agros nostros et vineas et domos nostras opponamus inopiæ nostræ, id est, venditioni seu impignorationi exponamus ad subveniendum nostræ indigentiæ. Ideo subditur, et accipiamus frumentum in fame, id est tempore famis seu caristiæ hujus. Et alii dicebant: Mutuo sumamus pecunias in tributa regis, id est, unus alteri concedat pecuniam ad usuram, ut persolvamus regi tributa, demusque agros nostros et vineas, exponendo eos (ut tactum est) venditioni vel impignorationi: quemadmodum in Genesi leguntur fecisse Ægyptii.
paras.en: [[5:2|And there were some that said: Our sons and our daughters are very many|Et erant qui dicerent: Filii nostri et filiæ nostræ multæ sunt nimis]], so that we cannot feed them: [[5:2|let us take up corn for the price of them, and let us eat and live|accipiamus pro pretio eorum frumentum, et comedamus et vivamus]], that is, let us sell them to the rich, and take food as their price. [[5:3|And there were some that said: Let us mortgage our lands, and our vineyards, and our houses|Et erant qui dicerent: Agros nostros et vineas et domos nostras opponamus]] to our want, that is, let us put them up for sale or pledge to relieve our need. Therefore it is added: [[5:3|and let us take corn because of the famine|et accipiamus frumentum in fame]], that is, in the time of this famine or dearth. [[5:4|And others said: Let us borrow money for the king's tribute|Et alii dicebant: Mutuo sumamus pecunias in tributa regis]], that is, let one grant another money at usury, so that we may pay the king's tributes, [[5:4|and let us give up our fields and vineyards|demusque agros nostros et vineas]], putting them up (as was touched on) for sale or pledge, as the Egyptians are read to have done in Genesis[[Gen 47:16||]][[Gen 47:17||]].

paras.t: Et nunc sicut carnes fratrum nostrorum, ita et carnes nostræ sunt, id est, corpora nostra merito essent a servitute aliena et libera, sicut et corpora divitum Judæorum, et ex eodem patriarcha Jacob sumus progeniti, ejusdemque legis ministri. Hinc in Joanne dixerunt Judæi: Semen Abrahæ sumus, et nemini unquam servivimus. Et sicut filii eorum, sunt liberi, ita et filii nostri merito liberi essent. Potest quoque exponi opposito modo: Sicut carnes fratrum nostrorum qui manserunt in Babylone, sunt in servitute sub rege Persarum, ita et nos sumus in afflictione: et idem de filiis illorum ac nostris.
paras.en: [[5:5|And now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren|Et nunc sicut carnes fratrum nostrorum, ita et carnes nostræ sunt]], that is, our bodies by right should be free and strangers to bondage, as the bodies of the rich Jews are, and we are sprung from the same patriarch Jacob, and are ministers of the same law. Hence the Jews said in John: [[John 8:33|We are the seed of Abraham: and we have never been slaves to any man|Semen Abrahæ sumus, et nemini unquam servivimus]]. And [[5:5|as their children|sicut filii eorum]] are free, [[5:5|and our children|ita et filii nostri]] by right should be free. It can also be expounded the opposite way: As the flesh of our brethren who stayed in Babylon is in bondage under the king of the Persians, so we too are in affliction: and the same of their children and ours.

paras.t: Et iratus sum nimis ira per zelum, præsertim contra divites qui se tam immisericorditer et avare habuerunt circa egenos. Cogitavitque cor meum mecum, id est, intra me deliberavi quid dicerem, nec ex impetu locutus sum passionis; et increpavi optimates et magistratus, id est superiores et judices Judæorum, dicens: Usurasne singuli a fratribus vestris egenis Judæis accipiatis? Tanquam dicerem: In hoc peccatis enormiter, quum in Deuteronomio jussum sit, Non fœnerabis fratri tuo ad usuram. Et congregavi adversus eos concionem, id est congregationem, magnam: quatenus publice corriperentur, qui publice peccaverunt, juxta illud Apostoli: Peccantes coram omnibus argue, ut et ceteri timorem habeant.
paras.en: [[5:6|And I was exceedingly angry|Et iratus sum nimis]] with the anger of zeal, above all against the rich, who behaved so unmercifully and avariciously towards the needy. [[5:7|And my heart thought with myself|Cogitavitque cor meum mecum]], that is, I considered within myself what I should say, and did not speak from an impulse of passion; [[5:7|and I rebuked the nobles and magistrates|et increpavi optimates et magistratus]], that is, the superiors and judges of the Jews, saying: [[5:7|Do you every one exact usury of your brethren|Usurasne singuli a fratribus vestris]], the needy Jews [Denis reads *accipiatis*, "receive"; a footnote of the edition gives *exigatis*, "exact", as the Vulgate has]? As if I were saying: In this you sin grievously, since it is commanded in Deuteronomy, [[Deut 23:19|Thou shalt not lend to thy brother|Non fœnerabis fratri tuo]] [[Deut 23:19|to usury|ad usuram]]. [[5:7|And I gathered together|Et congregavi]] [[5:7|against them|adversus eos]] an assembly, that is, a gathering, a great one: so that those who had sinned publicly might be publicly corrected, according to that of the Apostle: [[1 Tim 5:20|Them that sin reprove before all that the rest also may have fear.|Peccantes coram omnibus argue, ut et ceteri timorem habeant]]

paras.t: Et dixi eis: Nos, ut scitis, redemimus fratres nostros Judæos qui venditi fuerant gentibus, secundum possibilitatem nostram. Quamvis enim Cyrus rex Persarum et Artaxerxes rex dimiserunt Judæos gratis, quantum ad id juris, quod habuerunt in eos ratione captivitatis eorum in regnis suis, illi tamen Judæi qui venditi erant gentilibus, redimebantur ab his quorum servi emptitii erant. Sicque redemerunt multos eorum, ipse Zorobabel, Esdras et Nehemias. Et vos ergo vendetis fratres vestros, id est, Judæos quos emistis in servos, vendere vultis, non gratis dimittere, et nos ememus eos? quasi dicat: Non decet nec licet, præsertim in casu et tempore isto. Verumtamen absolute loquendo, non fuit Judæis prohibitum, filios suos ac filias vendere in famulos et ancillas, cogente penuria, Judæis divitibus. Nec divitibus illis fuit prohibitum emere illos, sed ultra sex annos ipsos tenere in servitute fuit prohibitum, juxta illud Exodi: Si emeris servum Hebræum, sex annis serviet tibi; in septimo egredietur liber gratis. Hinc a Jeremia arguuntur Judæi, quod talem libertatem non exhibuerunt servis emptitiis. Et siluerunt, nec invenerunt quid responderent: quia in isto casu generalis afflictionis atque inopiæ, debebant proximis suis egenis gratis misericorditer subvenire.
paras.en: [[5:8|And I said to them: We, as you know, have redeemed|Et dixi eis: Nos, ut scitis, redemimus]] [[5:8|our brethren the Jews, that were sold to the Gentiles|fratres nostros Judæos qui venditi fuerant gentibus]], [[5:8|according to our ability|secundum possibilitatem nostram]]. For although Cyrus king of the Persians[[1 Esd 1:2||]] and king Artaxerxes[[1 Esd 7:12||]] [the margin gives I Esdr. i, 2–4, and vii, 12–26] let the Jews go free, as regards the right they had over them by reason of their captivity in their kingdoms, yet those Jews who had been sold to gentiles were redeemed from those whose bought servants they were. And so Zorobabel himself, Esdras and Nehemias redeemed many of them. [[5:8|and will you then sell your brethren|Et vos ergo vendetis fratres vestros]], that is, do you wish to sell the Jews whom you have bought as servants, and not let them go free, [[5:8|for us to redeem them|et nos ememus eos]] [Denis reads *ememus*, "shall buy", for the Vulgate's *redimemus*]? As if to say: It is neither fitting nor lawful, especially in this case and at this time. Yet, speaking absolutely, the Jews were not forbidden, when want compelled them, to sell their sons and daughters as menservants and maidservants to rich Jews. Nor were those rich men forbidden to buy them; but to keep them in bondage beyond six years was forbidden, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 21:2|If thou buy a Hebrew servant, six years shall he serve thee; in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.|Si emeris servum Hebræum, sex annis serviet tibi; in septimo egredietur liber gratis]] Hence the Jews are rebuked by Jeremias because they did not grant such freedom to their bought servants[[Jer 34:9||]] [the margin gives Jer. xxxiv, 9–17].
