[[5:8|And they held their peace, and found not what to answer|Et siluerunt, nec invenerunt quid responderent]]: for in this case of general affliction and want they ought to have relieved their needy neighbours freely and mercifully.

paras.t: Et dixi eis: Non est bona res quam facitis. Quare non in timore Dei nostri filiali aut saltem initiali ambulatis, custodiendo divina præcepta? quia qui timet Deum, nihil negligit; ne exprobretur nobis ab inimicis nostris, id est, ne adversariis subjiciamur, et ne nobis insultent: juxta illud, Ne dicant inter gentes, Ubi est Deus eorum? Principaliter tamen Deum timere et honorare debemus ex caritate ipsius, quatenus ei complaceamus et uniamur. Istud dicendum est Christianis, ut scilicet timeant Deum, et obediant ei, ne exprobretur eis ab hostibus eorum, Turcis et Sarracenis.
paras.en: And I said to them: [[5:9|The thing you do is not good|Non est bona res quam facitis]]. [[5:9|why walk you not in the fear of our God|Quare non in timore Dei nostri]], with a filial or at least an initial fear [filial fear is a son's fear of offending a father he loves; initial fear, that of beginners, still mixed with fear of punishment], keeping God's commandments? For [[Eccles 7:19|he that feareth God, neglecteth nothing|qui timet Deum, nihil negligit]]; [[5:9|that we be not exposed to the reproaches of the Gentiles our enemies|ne exprobretur nobis ab inimicis nostris]], that is, lest we be made subject to our adversaries, and lest they insult us: according to that, [[Ps 78:10|Lest they should say among the Gentiles: Where is their God?|Ne dicant inter gentes, Ubi est Deus eorum?]] Yet principally we ought to fear and honour God out of charity towards him, so that we may please him and be united to him. This is to be said to Christians: that they should fear God and obey him, lest they be reproached by their enemies, the Turks and Saracens.

paras.t: Deinde Nehemias exemplo sui ipsius et suorum, hortatur Judæos ad liberalitatem et pietatem prætactas. Et ego et fratres mei et pueri mei domestici, commodavimus plurimis, id est, gratis concessimus multis Judæis pauperibus, pecuniam et frumentum. Non repetamus in commune istud, id est, communiter in hoc concordemus, quod ista sic mutuata, non repetantur ab eis qui facultatem non habent solvendi. Æs alienum concedamus quod debetur nobis, id est, pecuniam quæ nobis debetur a subditis ratione nostri ducatus, non exigimus nobis persolvi, sed quasi mutuatum quid relinquimus illis. Reddite ergo eis agros suos et vineas, etc. Quin potius et centesimam pecuniæ, id est centesimam partem pecuniæ, frumenti, vini et olei, quam exigere ab eis solebatis, date pro illis, id est, solvite pro ipsis pauperibus de bonis vestris, quum ipsi non habeant unde persolvant. Hæc centesima solvebatur regi pro tributo terræ. Insuper et excussi sinum meum, et dixi: Sic excutiat Dominus omnem virum, de quo loquor, qui non compleverit verbum istud, etc.
paras.en: Then Nehemias, by the example of himself and his household, exhorts the Jews to the liberality and kindness spoken of. [[5:10|Both I and my brethren, and my servants|Et ego et fratres mei et pueri mei]] of my household [[5:10|have lent|commodavimus]] [[5:10|to many|plurimis]], that is, have freely granted to many poor Jews, [[5:10|money and corn|pecuniam et frumentum]]. [[5:10|let us all agree not to call for it again|Non repetamus in commune istud]], that is, let us agree in common on this, that what has been lent in this way should not be called back from those who have no means of paying. [[5:10|let us forgive the debt that is owing to us|Æs alienum concedamus quod debetur nobis]], that is, the money which is owing to us from our subjects by reason of our governorship we do not require to be paid to us, but leave it to them as a thing lent. [[5:11|Restore ye to them|Reddite ergo eis]] [[5:11|their fields, and their vineyards|agros suos et vineas]], etc. [[5:11|and the hundredth part of the money|Quin potius et centesimam pecuniæ]], that is, the hundredth part of the money, [[5:11|and of the corn, the wine, and the oil, which you were wont to exact of them|frumenti, vini et olei, quam exigere ab eis solebatis]], [[5:11|give it rather for them|date pro illis]], that is, pay it for these poor men out of your own goods, since they have nothing to pay it with. This hundredth was paid to the king as tribute for the land. [[5:13|Moreover I shook my lap, and said|Insuper et excussi sinum meum, et dixi]]: [[5:13|So may God shake every man|Sic excutiat Dominus omnem virum]] of whom I speak, [[5:13|that shall not accomplish this word|qui non compleverit verbum istud]], etc.

paras.t: A die autem illa qua præceperat rex mihi, ut essem dux in terra Juda, id est per duodecim annos quibus præfui populo Judæorum ut dux, ex regis commissione, ego et fratres mei annonas non comedimus, id est, victum a populo non accepi, qui tamen mihi debebatur ratione ducatus mei, si exegissem. Quin potius in opere muri ædificavi propria manu interdum, et agrum non emi, quia propria commoda et divitias non quæsivi, sed Dei honorem et bonum commune.
paras.en: [[5:14|And from the day, in which the king commanded me to be governor in the land of Juda|A die autem illa qua præceperat rex mihi, ut essem dux in terra Juda]], that is, for the twelve years in which I was over the Jewish people as governor by the king's commission, [[5:14|I and my brethren did not eat the yearly allowance|ego et fratres mei annonas non comedimus]], that is, I did not take my keep from the people, which was nevertheless due to me by reason of my governorship, had I required it. [[5:16|Moreover I built in the work of the wall|Quin potius in opere muri ædificavi]], at times with my own hand, [[5:16|and I bought no land|et agrum non emi]], because I sought not my own advantage and riches, but God's honour and the common good.

paras.t: Judæi quoque et magistratus, centum quinquaginta viri, qui in officiis erant et a populo sustentari solebant, et qui veniebant ad nos de gentibus, in mensa mea erant: et sic fui hospes liberalis, ne populus gravaretur. Parabatur mihi, id est pro esu meo et eorum quos reficere volui, per dies singulos, id est quotidie, bos unus, arietes sex, et inter dies decem vina diversa, id est, plura dolia vinorum diversorum infra decem dies expendi cum commensalibus meis. Insuper et annonas ducatus mei non quæsivi. Valde enim attenuatus, id est per paupertatem exhaustus, erat populus pro majori parte. Memento mei, Deus meus, in bonum, id est ad hoc, ut mihi misericors sis et gratiose retribuas, secundum omnia quæ feci populo huic Judæorum, id est secundum merita beneficiorum quæ eis exhibui propter te; et sicut pie et liberaliter feci eis, ita fac mecum: juxta illud, Qua mensura mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis.
paras.en: [[5:17|The Jews also and the magistrates|Judæi quoque et magistratus]], [[5:17|one hundred and fifty men|centum quinquaginta viri]], who were in office and used to be maintained by the people, [[5:17|besides them that came to us from among the nations|et qui veniebant ad nos de gentibus]], [[5:17|were at my table|in mensa mea erant]]: and so I was a liberal host, so that the people should not be burdened. [[5:18|And there was prepared for me|Parabatur mihi]], that is, for my own eating and for those whom I wished to feed, [[5:18|day be day|per dies singulos]], that is, daily, [[5:18|one ox, and six choice rams|bos unus, arietes sex]], [[5:18|and once in ten days I gave store of divers wines|et inter dies decem vina diversa]], that is, within ten days I spent many casks of divers wines with those who sat at table with me. [[5:18|yet I did not require my yearly allowance as governor|Insuper et annonas ducatus mei non quæsivi]]. [[5:18|for the people were very much impoverished|valde enim attenuatus erat populus]], that is, worn out by poverty, for the most part. [[5:19|Remember me, O my God, for good|Memento mei, Deus meus, in bonum]], that is, to this end, that thou mayest be merciful to me and graciously reward me, [[5:19|according to all that I have done for this people|secundum omnia quæ feci populo huic]] of the Jews, that is, according to the merits of the benefits which I showed them for thy sake; and as I have dealt kindly and liberally with them, so deal thou with me: according to that, [[Matt 7:2|with what measure you mete, it shall be measured to you again|Qua mensura mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis]][[Luke 6:38||]].

paras.t: Ex isto capitulo ad opera pietatis instruimur; sed heu! jam multi infelicissimi nomine tenus Christiani, Judæorum avaritiam imitantur, usuras committunt, pauperes gravant, opprimuntque subjectos, filios suos ac filias vendunt servituti peccati, et subdunt jugo diaboli, non reprimendo eos a vitiis, sed magis inducendo ad vanitates. Docentur quoque majores prælati exemplo Nehemiæ, peccantes quamvis potentes et magnos, sine personarum acceptione strenue increpare, salubriter exhortari, atque ad condignam suorum exsecutionem officiorum seriosissime admonere. Imo omnes qui præsunt, docentur hic suis subditis in temporalibus et spiritualibus, præsertim inopiæ tempore liberaliter subvenire, non otio, loquacitati, voluptative gustus et tactus vacare; sed in omni opere virtuoso se ipsos in primis exemplares et alacres exhibere, et contentari sobrio cibo, modico potu, mediocrique somno.
paras.en: From this chapter we are taught works of mercy; but alas! now many most unhappy men, Christians in name only, imitate the avarice of the Jews, commit usury, burden the poor and oppress their subjects, sell their sons and daughters into the bondage of sin and put them under the devil's yoke, not restraining them from vices but rather leading them on to vanities. Greater prelates too are taught by the example of Nehemias to rebuke sinners vigorously, however powerful and great, without respect of persons[[1 Tim 5:20||]], to exhort them for their salvation, and to admonish them most earnestly to the worthy carrying out of their offices. Nay, all who are set over others are taught here to help their subjects liberally in temporal and spiritual things, above all in a time of want; not to give themselves to idleness, talk, or the pleasure of taste and touch; but to show themselves first of all a pattern and eager in every virtuous work, and to be content with sober food, little drink, and moderate sleep.

6.title: Explanatio capituli sexti: Factum est autem quum audisset Sanaballat
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: And it came to pass, when Sanaballat heard

paras.t: Describuntur hic insidiæ ipsi Nehemiæ illatæ.
paras.en: Here are described the plots laid against Nehemias himself.

paras.t: Factum est autem quum audisset Sanaballat et Tobias et Gossem, qui inter adversarios Nehemiæ erant principales, quod ædificassem murum, et non esset in ipso interruptio, quia jam erat integratus et continuatus; miserunt ad me, dicentes simulatorie: Veni, et percutiamus fœdus, id est, pactum pacis et amicitiæ ineamus firmissime: ideo additur, In vitulis, id est ipsum fœdus roborando per occisiones vitulorum, in signum quod morte dignus consisteret, qui pactum hoc violaret. Fuit namque antiquitus consuetudo, ut in confœderatione hujusmodi occideretur vitulus unus aut plures, aut alia pecora, in signum firmitatis, atque ad designandum quod mortem mereretur qui fœdus transgrederetur. Hinc per Jeremiam loquitur Dominus: Dabo viros qui prævaricantur fœdus meum, et non observaverunt verba fœderis, quibus assensi sunt in conspectu meo, vitulum quem conciderunt in duas partes, et transierunt inter divisiones illas. Ex quo elicitur, quod in signum firmitatis consueverunt etiam semel ire inter partes animalis occisi atque divisi. In campo uno. Volebant enim Nehemiam trahere extra urbem, quatenus in rure occiderent eum. Hinc subditur: Ipsi autem cogitabant ut facerent mihi malum. Deinde in littera ponitur excusatio Nehemiæ, et planus est textus.
paras.en: [[6:1|And it came to pass, when Sanaballat, and Tobias, and Gossem|Factum est autem quum audisset Sanaballat et Tobias et Gossem]], who were the chief among the adversaries of Nehemias, [[6:1|heard that I had built the wall|quod ædificassem murum]], [[6:1|and that there was no breach left in it|et non esset in ipso interruptio]], since it was now whole and continuous, they [[6:2|sent to me, saying|miserunt ad me, dicentes]] deceitfully: [[6:2|Come, and let us make a league together|Veni, et percutiamus fœdus]], that is, let us enter most firmly into a pact of peace and friendship: and so it is added, [[6:2|in the villages|In vitulis]] [Denis reads *in vitulis*, “with calves”, for *in viculis*, “in the villages”, which the margin gives], that is, strengthening the league itself by the slaying of calves, in sign that whoever broke this pact would be worthy of death. For it was the custom of old that in a league of this kind one calf or more, or other beasts, were slain in sign of its firmness, and to signify that whoever transgressed the league would deserve death. Hence the Lord speaks by Jeremias: [[Jer 34:18|And I will give the men that have transgressed my covenant, and have not performed the words of the covenant which they agreed to in my presence, when they cut the calf in two and passed between the parts thereof|Dabo viros qui prævaricantur fœdus meum, et non observaverunt verba fœderis, quibus assensi sunt in conspectu meo, vitulum quem conciderunt in duas partes, et transierunt inter divisiones illas]]. From which it is gathered that in sign of firmness they were also accustomed to pass once between the parts of the animal slain and divided. [[6:2|in the plain of Ono|In campo uno]] [Denis's text has *uno*, “one”; the margin gives *Ono*]. For they wished to draw Nehemias out of the city so as to kill him in the country. Hence it is added: [[6:2|But they thought to do me mischief|Ipsi autem cogitabant ut facerent mihi malum]]. Then the letter gives Nehemias's excuse, and the text is plain.

paras.t: Et immisit ad me Sanaballat, juxta verbum prius, id est insidiose, sicut et ante; non tamen verba præferentia speciem amicitiæ, sed comminationis. Aliquando tamen verba amicitiæ addidit simulatorie, sicut subjungitur: puerum, id est ministrum, et epistolam scriptam hoc modo: In gentibus auditum est, id est, inter nos gentiles jam publice vulgatum est, et Gossem, cui tanquam viro solenni credendum est, dixit, quod tu et Judæi cogitetis rebellare contra regem Persarum. Propter quam causam et prophetas posueris, qui prædicent de te in Jerusalem, id est, quosdam induxeris ad hoc, quod simulant se spiritum prophetiæ habere, dicentes quasi ex revelatione divina: Rex in Juda est, id est, ex Dei voluntate Nehemias iste est rex terræ et populi hujus: ideo ei, non regi Persarum, obediatis. Auditurus est rex hæc, id est, percipiet ista, et indignabitur tibi; idcirco veni, ut ineamus consilium pariter, qualiter possis te excusare. Et misi ad eos, dicens, specialiter ad Sanaballat, tanquam ad capitaneum iniquorum: Non est factum secundum verba hæc quæ loqueris per epistolam quam misisti. Quam ob causam magis confortavi manus meas, id est, tanto plus animavi me ad operandum, quanto multiplicius ac insidiosius impius ille volebat me impedire. Sic et nos debemus tanto ferventius Deo servire, vitiisque resistere, quanto importunius invisibiles adversarii nos impugnant, aut homines pravi impedire nostrum profectum nituntur.
paras.en: [[6:5|And Sanaballat sent|Et immisit ad me Sanaballat]] to me, [[6:5|according to the former word|juxta verbum prius]], that is, treacherously, as before; yet not with words that bore a show of friendship, but of threatening. Yet sometimes he added words of friendship deceitfully, as follows: [[6:5|his servant|puerum]], that is, his minister, [[6:5|and he had a letter in his hand written in this manner|et epistolam scriptam hoc modo]]: [[6:6|It is reported amongst the Gentiles|In gentibus auditum est]], that is, it is now publicly spread abroad among us gentiles, [[6:6|and Gossem hath said it|et Gossem dixit]], who as a man of weight is to be believed, [[6:6|that thou and the Jews think to rebel|quod tu et Judæi cogitetis rebellare]] against the king of the Persians. [[6:6|for which end|Propter quam causam]] [[6:7|Thou hast also set up prophets|et prophetas posueris]], [[6:7|to preach of thee at Jerusalem|qui prædicent de te in Jerusalem]], that is, thou hast induced certain men to pretend that they have the spirit of prophecy, [[6:7|saying|dicentes]] as if by divine revelation: [[6:7|There is a king in Judea|Rex in Juda est]], that is, by the will of God this Nehemias is king of this land and people: therefore obey him, not the king of the Persians. [[6:7|The king will hear of these things|Auditurus est rex hæc]], that is, he will learn of them, and will be angry with thee; [[6:7|therefore come now, that we may take counsel together|idcirco veni, ut ineamus consilium pariter]], how thou mayest excuse thyself. [[6:8|And I sent to them, saying|Et misi ad eos, dicens]], to Sanaballat especially, as to the captain of the wicked: [[6:8|There is no such thing done as thou sayest|Non est factum secundum verba hæc quæ loqueris]] in the letter thou hast sent. [[6:9|Wherefore I strengthened my hands the more|Quam ob causam magis confortavi manus meas]], that is, I spurred myself on to the work the more, the more manifoldly and treacherously that wicked man wished to hinder me. So we too ought to serve God and resist vices the more fervently, the more importunately our invisible adversaries assail us, or wicked men strive to hinder our progress.

paras.t: Et ingressus sum domum Semaiæ Judæi, quem mihi fidelem esse putavi, qui ait: Tractemus nobiscum in domo Dei, id est inter nos conferamus in templo, qualiter tu, Nehemia, evadere possis pericula, et claudamus portas ædis, id est domus Dei, ut intra templum maneas clausus; quia venturi sunt Sanaballat et sui, ut interficiant te. Et dixi, refutando talem suggestionem: Num quisquam similis mei fugit? id est, numquid aliquis in Deo confidens, et quæ Dei sunt agens, fugere habet timore humano? Et quis ut ego, id est, quis similis mei in Dei confidentia, ingredietur templum fugiendo hostes, et vivet? ac si dicat: Si sic fugeret timore inordinato, mereretur divino privari auxilio, et occidi. Nihilominus licitum est ex rationabili causa, et ex naturali mortis timore, præsidium fugæ assumere, et locum sacrum ac tutum intrare, sicut et David sanctus frequenter fugit a facie Saul. Non tamen id licitum est in derogationem justitiæ, atque in detrimentum boni communis, sicut in proposito isto. Ad hoc enim falsarius iste voluit Nehemiam in templo recludere, ut opus Dei negligeretur, et Nehemias notaretur de fuga formidolosa, quasi non sperans in Domino.
paras.en: [[6:10|And I went into the house of Samaia|Et ingressus sum domum Semaiæ]] the Jew, whom I thought faithful to me, who said: [[6:10|Let us consult together in the house of God|Tractemus nobiscum in domo Dei]], that is, let us confer together in the temple how thou, Nehemias, mayest escape the dangers, [[6:10|and let us shut the doors of the temple|et claudamus portas ædis]], that is, of the house of God, so that thou mayest stay shut up within the temple; [[6:10|for they will come to kill thee|quia venturi sunt ut interficiant te]], Sanaballat and his men. [[6:11|And I said|Et dixi]], refuting such a suggestion: [[6:11|Should such a man as I flee?|Num quisquam similis mei fugit?]] that is, should anyone who trusts in God and does the things of God flee out of human fear? [[6:11|and who is there that being as I am|Et quis ut ego]], that is, who that is like me in trust in God, [[6:11|would go into the temple, to save his life?|ingredietur templum fugiendo hostes, et vivet?]] fleeing from the enemy; as if to say: if he fled so out of inordinate fear, he would deserve to be deprived of divine help and to be slain. Nevertheless it is lawful, for a reasonable cause and from the natural fear of death, to take the protection of flight and to enter a holy and safe place, as holy David too often fled from the face of Saul. But it is not lawful to the prejudice of justice and to the detriment of the common good, as in the case before us. For this forger wished to shut Nehemias up in the temple so that the work of God would be neglected, and Nehemias would be branded with a fearful flight, as though he did not hope in the Lord.

paras.t: Et intellexi, ex divino instinctu seu consideratione industriæ meæ, quod Deus non misisset eum, id est, ex divina directione mihi talia non proferret. Sicque de spirituali, non locali, missione intelligitur istud, quemadmodum tertio Regum Ahias senex et cæcus dixit ad uxorem Jeroboam ad se missam: Ego missus sum ad te durus nuntius. Sed quasi vaticinans, id est non vere, sed apparenter prophetans, locutus esset ad me. Magis enim debuerat consulere Nehemiæ, ut confidendo in Domino, præpararet se ad resistendum adversariis illis divini cultus ac boni communis, quam ut ita recluderet se. Acceperat enim pretium, id est pecuniam a Sanaballat, ut ita deciperet me, et haberent malum, id est, aliquam culpam scirent de me, quod exprobrarent, id est, insultarent atque objicerent, mihi. Memento mei, Domine, pro Tobia et Sanaballat, id est, a talibus erue me, juxta opera eorum talia, ut eis pœnam justam infligas, propter tam vitiosa verba eorum et gesta. Mihi autem miserearis, eo quod tanta ac talia ab ipsis injuste perpessus sim. Sed et Noadiæ prophetæ et ceterorum prophetarum qui terrebant me, id est, illorum pseudoprophetarum volentium me perterrere, memento per debitam eorum castigationem saltem in vita hac, ne pereant in æternum.
paras.en: [[6:12|And I understood that God had not sent him|Et intellexi quod Deus non misisset eum]], by a divine prompting or by my own careful consideration: that is, that he was not putting such things to me by divine direction. And so this is understood of a spiritual, not a local, sending, as in the third book of Kings Ahias, old and blind, said to the wife of Jeroboam, who had been sent to him: [[3 Kings 14:6|I am sent to thee with heavy tidings|Ego missus sum ad te durus nuntius]]. [[6:12|but that he had spoken to me as if he had been prophesying|sed quasi vaticinans locutus esset ad me]], that is, not truly but in appearance prophesying. For he ought rather to have counselled Nehemias, trusting in the Lord, to prepare himself to resist those adversaries of the divine worship and of the common good, than so to shut himself up. [[6:13|For he had taken money|Acceperat enim pretium]], that is, money from Sanaballat, to deceive me so, [[6:13|and they might have some evil|et haberent malum]], that is, might know of some fault in me, [[6:13|to upbraid me withal|quod exprobrarent mihi]], that is, to insult me with and cast up at me. [[6:14|Remember me, O Lord, for Tobias and Sanaballat|Memento mei, Domine, pro Tobia et Sanaballat]], that is, deliver me from such men, [[6:14|according to their works of this kind|juxta opera eorum talia]], so that thou mayest inflict just punishment on them for their so vicious words and deeds; but have mercy on me, because I have unjustly suffered so many and such things from them. [[6:14|and Noadias the prophet, and the rest of the prophets that would have put me in fear|Sed et Noadiæ prophetæ et ceterorum prophetarum qui terrebant me]], that is, of those false prophets who wished to terrify me, remember them by their due chastisement, at least in this life, lest they perish for ever.

paras.t: Completus est autem murus Jerusalem vicesimo quinto die mensis Elul: qui dicitur esse sextus mensis apud Judæos, ac correspondere communiter partim nostro Augusto, et partim Septembri; quinquaginta duobus diebus. Quo constat, quam ferventer ac fortiter laboraverunt. Unde de tam expedita et celeri consummatione muri, consternati sunt adversarii, videntes hoc fieri non potuisse absque speciali Omnipotentis subsidio. Et hoc est quod subditur: Factum est autem quum audissent, etc.
paras.en: [[6:15|But the wall was finished the five and twentieth day of the month of Elul|Completus est autem murus Jerusalem vicesimo quinto die mensis Elul]], which is said to be the sixth month among the Jews, and to correspond commonly partly to our August and partly to September; [[6:15|in two and fifty days|quinquaginta duobus diebus]]. From which it is clear how fervently and strongly they laboured. Hence at so speedy and swift a completion of the wall the adversaries were dismayed, seeing that it could not have been done without the special help of the Almighty. And this is what is added: [[6:16|And it came to pass when all our enemies heard of it|Factum est autem quum audissent]], etc.

paras.t: Sed et in diebus illis multæ optimatum Judæorum epistolæ mittebantur ad Tobiam, id est, multi majores inter Judæos miserunt frequenter epistolas ad Tobiam, Samaritanum habitatione, sed Ammoniten natione, ut patet supra; et a Tobia veniebant ad eos epistolæ. Multi enim erant in Juda habentes juramentum ejus, id est, confœderati ei cum jurejurando, quia gener erat, id est, filiam habuit Secheniæ in uxorem: qui Sechenias fuit unus de præcipuis inter Judæos; et Johanan filius ejus, puta Tobiæ, acceperat filiam Mosollam inter Judæos notabilis viri. Sicque per conjugia fuit inter istos Judæos et Samaritanos amicitia et confœderatio facta: quod periculosum fuit Nehemiæ, quum non sit nequior pestis, quam hostis familiaris, cui dum creditur, periculum improvise incurritur. Tamen quod dictum est, Johanan filius ejus, ad Secheniam posset referri. Sed et laudabant eum, puta Tobiam, coram me, ut inirem pactum cum illo. Et verba mea nuntiabant ei secrete per scripta seu nuntios.
paras.en: [[6:17|Moreover in those days many letters were sent by the principal men of the Jews to Tobias|Sed et in diebus illis multæ optimatum Judæorum epistolæ mittebantur ad Tobiam]], that is, many of the greater men among the Jews often sent letters to Tobias, a Samaritan by dwelling but an Ammonite by nation, as is plain above[[2 Esd 4:3||]]; [[6:17|and from Tobias there came letters to them|et a Tobia veniebant ad eos epistolæ]]. [[6:18|For there were many in Judea sworn to him|Multi enim erant in Juda habentes juramentum ejus]], that is, leagued with him by oath, [[6:18|because he was the son in law|quia gener erat]], that is, he had the daughter of Sechenias to wife, which Sechenias was one of the chief men among the Jews; [[6:18|and Johanan his son had taken to wife the daughter of Mosollam|et Johanan filius ejus, puta Tobiæ, acceperat filiam Mosollam]], namely Tobias's son, the daughter of a notable man among the Jews. And so through marriages friendship and alliance were made between these Jews and the Samaritans: which was dangerous for Nehemias, since there is no worse plague than an enemy of one's own household, for while he is trusted, danger is run into unawares. Yet what is said, *Johanan his son*, could be referred to Sechenias. [[6:19|And they praised him also before me|Sed et laudabant eum, puta Tobiam, coram me]], namely Tobias, so that I would make a pact with him. [[6:19|and they related my words to him|Et verba mea nuntiabant ei]] secretly by writings or messengers.

paras.t: Unde constat, quam verissime scriptum sit, Multæ tribulationes justorum: quia Nehemiam justum qui tam beneficus et liberalissimus fuit in suos, imo in totum populum Judæorum, tantaque bona exhibuit eis, et pro communi eorum bono tam infatigabiliter laboravit, ita sunt persecuti, non solum Samaritani et alieni, sed et populus ejus et notabiliores eorum. Patientiam ergo discamus, nec propter quamcumque persecutionem a via justitiæ recedamus, confidentes semper in Domino. Innotescit demum ex introductis, quod Judæi post reditum a Babylonica captivitate cito recesserunt a Domino pro magna parte: imo multa magna commiserunt peccata, ac profana contraxerunt contra legem connubia.
paras.en: Hence it is clear how very truly it is written: [[Ps 33:20|Many are the afflictions of the just|Multæ tribulationes justorum]]: for the just Nehemias, who was so beneficent and most liberal towards his own, nay towards the whole people of the Jews, and showed them so many good things, and laboured so tirelessly for their common good, was so persecuted not only by the Samaritans and strangers but by his own people and the more notable of them. Let us learn patience, then, and not depart from the way of justice for any persecution, trusting always in the Lord[[Jer 17:7||]]. Lastly, it becomes known from what has been brought in that the Jews, after their return from the Babylonian captivity, soon fell away from the Lord in great part: indeed they committed many great sins, and contracted unholy marriages against the law.

7.title: Expositio capituli septimi: Postquam autem ædificatus est murus
7.title_en: Exposition of the seventh chapter: Now after the wall was built

paras.t: Sententia hujus capituli quasi tota contenta est supra. Præmittitur tamen hic aliquid, quod ibi non legitur.
paras.en: The substance of this chapter is almost wholly contained above[[1 Esd 2:1||]]. Yet something is set first here which is not read there.

paras.t: Postquam autem ædificatus est murus Jerusalem, prout præcedenti habetur capitulo, et posui valvas, id est portas seu januas, in portarum structuris seu in templo, et recensui, id est numeravi, janitores et cantores templi, et Levitas; et dixi: Non aperiantur portæ Jerusalem usque ad calorem solis, id est, quousque sol notabiliter super nostrum horizontem ascendat, ita quod calor ex reflexione radiorum solarium causetur in terra. Quumque adhuc adsisterent mihi viri, quibus hæc dixi, portæ Jerusalem clausæ sunt ante solis occasum, et oppilatæ, id est obturatæ ad insultum hostium repellendum. Nam pauci adhuc in Jerusalem morabantur. Et posui custodes ad vigilandum per noctes, secundum vices suas et ex opposito domorum suarum in muro. Et non erant domus ædificatæ ad sufficientiam.
paras.en: [[7:1|Now after the wall was built|Postquam autem ædificatus est murus]] of Jerusalem, as we have it in the preceding chapter[[2 Esd 6:15||]], [[7:1|and I had set up the doors|et posui valvas]], that is, the gates or doors, in the structures of the gates or in the temple, [[7:1|and numbered the porters and singing men, and Levites|et recensui janitores, et cantores, et Levitas]] of the temple; [[7:3|And I said to them|et dixi]]: [[7:3|Let not the gates of Jerusalem be opened till the sun be hot|Non aperiantur portæ Jerusalem usque ad calorem solis]], that is, until the sun has risen well above our horizon, so that heat is caused on the earth by the reflection of the sun's rays. [[7:3|And while they were yet standing by|Quumque adhuc adsisterent]] me, the men to whom I said this, [[7:3|the gates were shut|portæ Jerusalem clausæ sunt]] before sunset, [[7:3|and barred|et oppilatæ]], that is, blocked up to repel an assault of the enemy. For few as yet dwelt in Jerusalem. [[7:3|and I set watchmen|Et posui custodes]] to keep watch by night, [[7:3|every one by their courses, and every man over against his house|secundum vices suas et ex opposito domorum suarum]] on the wall. [[7:4|and the houses were not built|Et non erant domus ædificatæ]] in sufficient number.

paras.t: Deus autem dedit in corde meo, id est, inspiravit mihi ut facerem quod subditur: et congregavi optimates et magistratus et vulgus, ut recenserem eos, id est numerarem, sicque disponerem de populatione urbis Jerusalem; et inveni librum census, id est numerationis, eorum qui ascenderant primum, id est, cum Zorobabel de Babylonia redierunt in prima licentia a Cyro data, et inventum est scriptum in eo, id est in libro illo: Isti filii provinciæ qui ascenderunt de captivitate, etc. Ista verba scripta sunt ab Esdra, ibique exposita, eademque summa totius multitudinis hic et ibi exprimitur; sed quædam nomina variantur, quoniam multi eorum duo aut plura nomina habuerunt.
paras.en: [[7:5|But God had put in my heart|Deus autem dedit in corde meo]], that is, inspired me to do what follows: [[7:5|and I assembled the princes and magistrates, and common people|et congregavi optimates et magistratus et vulgus]], [[7:5|to number them|ut recenserem eos]], that is, to count them, and so to make arrangements for peopling the city of Jerusalem; [[7:5|and I found a book of the number of them who came up at first|et inveni librum census, id est numerationis, eorum qui ascenderant primum]], that is, who returned from Babylonia with Zorobabel under the first leave given by Cyrus, [[7:5|and therein it was found written|et inventum est scriptum in eo]], that is, in that book: [[7:6|These are the children of the province, who came up from the captivity|Isti filii provinciæ qui ascenderunt de captivitate]], etc. These words were written by Esdras[[1 Esd 2:1||]] and expounded there, and the same total of the whole multitude is given here and there; but some names vary, since many of them had two or more names.

paras.t: Nonnulli autem de principibus familiarum dederunt in opus. Hoc est quod supra scriptum est: Et de principibus patrum, quum ingrederentur templum Domini quod est in Jerusalem, sponte obtulerunt in domum Dei ad exstruendam eam in impensas operis auri solidos sexaginta millia, etc. Verumtamen quæ ibi dicuntur quasi in generali, hic specialius exprimuntur: et ita quantum ad particulares descriptiones, differentia invenitur inter verba hujus passus atque illius.
paras.en: [[7:70|And some of the heads of the families gave unto the work|Nonnulli autem de principibus familiarum dederunt in opus]]. This is what was written above: [[1 Esd 2:68|And some of the chief of the fathers, when they came to the temple of the Lord, which is in Jerusalem, offered freely to the house of the Lord to build it|Et de principibus patrum, quum ingrederentur templum Domini quod est in Jerusalem, sponte obtulerunt in domum Dei ad exstruendam eam]], [[1 Esd 2:69|they gave towards the expenses of the work|in impensas operis]] sixty thousand solids of gold, etc. Yet what is said there as it were in general is set out here more particularly: and so, as regards the particular descriptions, a difference is found between the words of this passage and of that.
